info.title: RChat API
info.description:
RChat is a self-hosted chat server: servers with text and voice channels, roles and per-channel permissions, threads, direct messages with calls, media uploads, link previews and search. This document covers version 1 of the REST API plus the `/.well-known` discovery documents.

**Versions.** `/api/v1/...` is version 1. `/api/...` without a version uses the latest version.

**Authentication.** Register or log in to get a session token and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Endpoints marked with an optional security requirement also work without a token for guests, when the instance has guest access turned on (`guests_enabled` in `GET /api/v1/settings`); otherwise they answer 401. On endpoints that need a token, `401 Unauthorized` means the token is missing or unknown. When the token cannot be checked (the database is unavailable), any endpoint that reads it answers `503 {"error": "Cannot check your session right now. Try again soon"}`: keep the token and retry. Servers may opt in to guest text and voice when enabled by the site. Password-protected servers additionally need a guest grant from `POST /api/v1/servers/{name}/guest_access`, sent in the `X-Guest-Grant` header (comma-separated, up to 100 grants).

**Audit reasons.** A request that changes something may say why in an `X-Audit-Reason` header (percent-encoded UTF-8, at most 300 characters). Every server audit log entry the request writes keeps it as `reason` in its details.

**Names.** Server names and usernames are case-insensitive: they are matched by their lowercase form, and responses carry the lowercase `name`/`username` alongside `display_name`: a server's name in its original case, or the name a user shows, which starts as the username as registered and can change. Only usernames are used for mentions and sign-in.

**Timestamps** are Unix time in seconds unless a field says otherwise.

**Pagination.** List endpoints return a JSON array. When more items follow, the `X-Next-Cursor` response header holds an opaque cursor; pass it back as the `cursor` query parameter for the next page. The header is absent on the last page. Each endpoint lists its page size and limits.

**Rate limits.** Every `/api` route except `/api/v1/health` and `/api/v1/ready` shares a general per-client-IP bucket (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND`, default 10 per second, burst `RATE_LIMIT_BURST`, default 60). The `/.well-known` routes have their own general bucket of the same size, separate from the `/api` one. Register, login, OIDC start, callback and exchange, word hints, recovery challenges, recovery sign-in, password change, backup phrase changes, guest access, server name checks, config links, P2P identity bindings, P2P backup uploads and deletes, sending and exporting reports, and media upload also share a strict per-IP bucket (`RATE_LIMIT_STRICT_PER_SECOND`, default 2 per second, burst `RATE_LIMIT_STRICT_BURST`, default 30). Invite previews, joining a server and the webhook execution routes each have their own per-IP bucket (`RATE_LIMIT_INVITE_PER_SECOND` and `RATE_LIMIT_INVITE_BURST`, by default the strict bucket's size); with `REDIS_URL` set, the invite preview and join buckets count across copies. Exceeding a bucket answers `429 {"error": "Too Many Requests! Wait for ns", "reason": {"kind": "rate", "retry_after": n}}` with `Retry-After: n` (whole seconds, rounded up). Messages each account sends (channel, thread and DM messages, forwards and polls, and switches of encrypted storage, which post a system message), and guest text per client address, count in a bucket of `MESSAGE_RATE_BURST` (default 100) that refills `MESSAGE_RATE_PER_MINUTE` a minute (default 2400), across copies when `REDIS_URL` is set; past it the answer is `429 {"error": "Sending too fast, try again in a moment", "reason": {"kind": "rate", "retry_after": n}}` with `Retry-After`. Requests a person makes a few times a day at most (sign-ups, new display names, password changes, backup phrase changes, recovery, server name checks, new, renamed and deleted servers, server passwords, webhooks and their secrets and tests, config links, P2P backups and P2P bindings) are rare requests: each kind counts per account, or per client address for sign-ups and recovery, at most `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR` (20) an hour and `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_DAY` (100) a day by default. Password and backup phrase changes count only once the current password or phrase is confirmed. Past them the answer is `429 {"error": "You've done this too often. Try again later.", "reason": {"kind": "rate", "retry_after": n}}` with `Retry-After`.

**Errors.** Errors raised by the API come as JSON `{"error": "..."}` (`ApiErrorBody`). Many also carry `reason`, an object for programs: `kind` says what happened (`off_site`: turned off for this site; `off_account`: turned off for your account; `off_server`: turned off in this server; `off_app` and `app`: an app's setting or rule; `limit`: you reached a limit; `capacity`: the site is full right now; `invalid`: a value is wrong; `rate`: too many requests; `conflict`: someone else changed it or the name is taken; `sign_in`: the session ended; `unavailable`: the server can't do it right now; `locked`: a moderator locked it; `confirm`: confirm first; `forced`: this site requires it; `keys`: this site has no encryption key ready), `control` names the setting or limit (for `confirm`, what to confirm), `retry_after` is the wait in seconds (also sent as the `Retry-After` header), `field` names the wrong value, `until` is when a lock ends (unix seconds) and `channel` the channel a `confirm` opens. Status codes and `error` texts are the same with and without it. An error without `reason` is a denial about a server, channel or message you cannot open, or an error that has no kind yet. When the database does not answer in time, an endpoint answers `503 {"error": "Server busy, try again in a moment", "reason": {"kind": "unavailable", "retry_after": 1}}` with `Retry-After: 1`: retry the request. Any other server error is `500 {"error": "Something went wrong"}`. Malformed JSON bodies are rejected by the framework with a plain-text 400, 415 or 422.

**Private servers stay hidden.** A password-protected server is indistinguishable from one that does not exist to anyone without access (membership, a valid guest grant, or the password where an endpoint takes one). Every endpoint that takes a server name answers both with the same `404 {"error": "Server not found or wrong password"}`; endpoints that take a password (`join`, `guest_access`, invites) answer a missing password with the same `401 {"error": "Password required"}` and a wrong one with that 404, and always hash the password, also for names that do not exist. Endpoints that take a channel or message id answer `404 {"error": "Not found"}` for ids that do not exist, that you cannot see (hidden channels, messages before your join without read history) or that belong to a server you cannot access. Bans are only reported (403) once access was proven. Servers people join with an invite (`join_mode` `invite`) and closed servers are hidden the same way, under a random key. While the instance's `server_joining` (`GET /api/v1/settings`) is `invites` or `nobody`, a server without a password is hidden in the same way from everyone who is not a member, signed in or not, and under `nobody` a missing password gets the 404 too. `GET /api/v1/servers/{name}/available` is the one deliberate existence check, because creating a server reveals the same.

**Realtime.** `GET /api/v1/ws` upgrades to a WebSocket. Clients send JSON frames tagged by `type` (`auth` first, with the token or without one for a guest, then `viewing`, `subscribe`, voice, call and `rtc_signal` frames) and receive JSON events tagged by `type` in snake_case (`message`, `message_updated`, `message_deleted`, `member_joined`, `presence_changed`, `read_updated`, `ping`, `ping_count`, `voice_state`, `call_state` and more; see `WsEvent` in `apps/server/src/ws/event.rs`). `ping` (`{username, ping: Ping}`) reaches only the pinged user's connections when someone mentions them; `ping_count` (`{username, scope, pings, pings_until, thread_pings}`, same fields as a `GET /api/v1/unreads` item) gives a scope's unseen pings after some were removed. `@everyone`, `@here` and role mentions send no per-user event: the `message` event carries `group_mentions`, each client decides whether the message addresses it (member, online, holds the role). `group_pings_seen` (`{username, scope, message_ids}`) tells the user's connections that `POST /api/v1/inbox/read` or `POST /api/v1/inbox/read_all` marked those group mentions seen. A signed-in user is online while any of their connections is open, whatever server or page it shows (unless they appear offline), and goes offline about 10 seconds after the last one closes. Switching to appear offline hides them at once; coming back online is allowed a few times in a row, then about once per 10 seconds, and the last setting wins. An account keeps at most `WS_CONNECTIONS_PER_USER` connections (default 20; opening another closes the oldest with close code 4008), and opening them faster than `WS_CONNECT_BURST` / `WS_CONNECTS_PER_MINUTE` (counted per instance and across the cluster) closes the new one with code 4029. One client address keeps at most `WS_SOCKETS_PER_IP` connections per instance (default 200; past it the upgrade answers 429) and `WS_GUEST_SOCKETS_PER_IP` of them as guests (default 50; past it the guest connection closes with code 4029); an IPv6 /64 counts as one address. All guest connections of one instance together are capped at `WS_GUEST_SOCKETS_MAX` (default 2000, 0 turns guest connections off; past it the guest connection closes with code 4029). All connections of one copy together are capped at `WS_SOCKETS_MAX` (default no cap; past it the upgrade answers 503 with reason `capacity`, and `/api/v1/ready` answers 503 with `sockets: false`). A connection that sends no `auth` frame within 10 seconds closes with code 4001. `subscribe` frames are paced per connection by the number of servers they newly check (at most 100 servers per frame, 50 for guests); one past the pace waits and a later one replaces it. `voice_join` and `voice_leave` are paced per account (a few per second; the latest waits and wins), `call_start` and `call_accept` too (each on its own), and `rtc_signal` payloads are at most 20 KiB with a per-account byte budget (enough to negotiate with a full voice room twice at once); past these the server answers an `error` frame (`{message}`, plus the `reason` object of REST errors when the error has one). These paces count per server process. `voice_join` may carry `muted` and `deafened`, what the joiner says about its own mic and sound, and `voice_audio` (`{muted, deafened}`) changes them for the voice seat that connection holds (ignored without one); accounts, guests and voice frames may send it, paced per account on its own (a few per second; the latest waits and wins). Listeners of the channel get each change as `voice_audio` (`{server, channel_id, username, muted, deafened}`); the `voice_state` of the snapshot a connection gets on opening or subscribing lists the room's users not at the default in `audio`. `presence_changed` (`{server, username, online, online_count}`) reaches the connections viewing that server when a member's first connection opens or last one closes, and when members join, leave, are kicked or banned, and `GET /api/v1/unreads` lists the unread ones as `group_pings`. `layout_changed` (`{server, layout}`, a `ChannelLayout`) carries the new channel order, with only the channels each connection can see and only the categories holding one of them (all categories for people who manage channels); a connection that doesn't manage channels gets it only when the part it sees changed. A connection without read history of a channel gets no events about a thread whose root was sent before it joined: no replies, edits, reactions, deletions, link previews or typing there. In a server that keeps its members to itself, connections from outside get no `message_deleted` or `messages_deleted` ids of `join` and `leave` messages. Every `position` a client gets (channels and categories, in REST answers and events) counts only what that client can see, so it runs 0, 1, 2 and so on without gaps. `read_updated` (`{username, scope, last_read, pings_until}`) tells the reader's other connections that `POST /api/v1/read` (or, once per scope, `POST /api/v1/read/batch`) stored a position or marked pings seen; clients clear only pings with an id up to `pings_until` (0: none), so newer pings keep their badge. The REST operations below name the events they emit.

post.summary: Open a private channel as the instance
post.description:
Opens a private channel to the site admin. Everyone else, and every channel that does not
exist, gets the same 404. A channel that only instance powers open (its rules hide it from
the admin's own membership, or the admin is no member) answers 403 `Confirm to open this
channel` with `reason.control` `staff_view` on every route until this request confirms. It
checks `reauth` (`fresh_session` is refused), writes a `staff.view_channel` entry to the
instance audit log and opens the channel for `CHANNEL_OPEN_SECS`; after that the 403 comes
back. A channel the admin's own membership views without read history reads as it does for
members until this request confirms it, which opens its whole history the same way. A
channel the admin's own membership opens fully needs none of this, and no entry is written
for it. The optional `X-Staff-Reason` header (at most 512 characters,
percent-encoded UTF-8) is kept with the entry, here and on every other request that writes
a staff entry. When the entry can't be written the answer is 503 and nothing opens. The
admin's own connections get `staff_view_opened`, so their WS delivers the channel's events
until it closes.

Checks the username and password (or words) and returns a new session token; existing
sessions stay valid. The account is the one with that username in any case, else the one
account whose username the name passes for in look-alike characters; a name that passes for
several accounts fails like a wrong password. Each account, whatever name reaches it, admits
one login or recovery attempt every 3 seconds and at most 1000 login and recovery attempts
per UTC day (successful ones included); after that it is locked until the next UTC day. Each
look-alike key of the name given is paced and counted the same way, and an attempt is admitted
only when the account and every key admit it. Names over 100 characters answer 401 at once.
Throttled attempts are not checked. No authentication. Strict and general rate-limit buckets.

post.summary: Sign in with a backup phrase
post.description:
Proves the account's backup phrase with a signature over a challenge from
`POST /api/v1/auth/recovery/challenge` (purpose `recover`, empty context), replaces the password
or words, and returns a new session token. Every other session of the account is revoked and
its WebSocket connections close. The backup phrase stays set. The account is found as by
`POST /api/v1/auth/login`, look-alike names included; the signature covers the name as the
challenge returned it. An unknown account, a name that passes for several accounts, one without
a backup phrase, a used, expired or foreign nonce and a wrong signature all answer the same
401. Recovery and login share each account's pace: one attempt every 3 seconds and at most
1000 a UTC day, for the account and every look-alike key of the name given. An
invalid new password answers 400 and leaves the nonce unused. New words come from the word
set of the name given and of the account; words outside the account's set answer 400 only
after the signature is checked, with the nonce used up. No authentication. Strict and general
rate-limit buckets.
Recovery challenges and recovery sign-ins are rare requests of one kind: at most
`RARE_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR` (20) an hour and `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_DAY` (100) a day per client address
(an IPv6 /64 counts as one) by default, whatever the username. A sign-in refused by the pace or
the daily lock (429, 423) does not count.

post.description:
Blocks `username` for the signed-in user. A blocked user can no longer open a new DM with you,
send, edit, react or pin in your DM, call you or answer your call (`403` with the same text a
user who does not accept messages gives), a call between you that is ringing or active ends
(`call_state` ended, the call log is finalized), and nothing they do pings you: mentions,
replies and reactions from them are dropped, and their unseen pings are removed (`ping_count`).
Your DM with them is closed (`dm_closed`, read up to its newest message) and does not reopen on
their messages. You can not message, edit, react, pin or call in that DM either until you
unblock them. Blocking is private: the blocked user gets no event and no answer tells them.
Emits `user_blocked` (`{username, user, blocked_at}`) to your connections when the user was not
blocked yet; blocking again changes nothing. At most 1000 blocked users. Each call counts,
also for a name with no account: 120 blocks per 10 minutes per account, apart from new DMs
and friend requests. A name with no account, and an account whose profile card you may not
see, also count as a miss (`LOOKUP_MISSES_PER_HOUR`, as for `GET
/api/v1/users/{username}/card`); past the misses every block is refused until the hour ends.
Requires a bearer token. General rate-limit bucket.

Either participant switches it. From then on new messages, edits and polls of the DM are
stored encrypted with a key this site keeps, or plain again. Messages stored before stay as
they were, and turning it off decrypts nothing. This is not end-to-end encryption. A change

a request counts as a message against the message rate, and a block between the
participants refuses it like a message.

instance, for the audience named in `aud`. The audience verifies it with the keys at
`/.well-known/jwks.json` of the issuer. Requires a bearer token; guests can't call it. No
side effects. General rate-limit bucket.

post.summary: Bind a P2P identity key to your account
post.description:
Signs a JWT (7 days) stating that the caller, `username@host` on this instance, holds the P2P
identity key `ik`. Peers show it as an account badge after checking it against the keys at
`/.well-known/jwks.json`. The proof is a signature by `ik` itself, so nobody can bind a key
they don't hold. An identity made with a backup phrase sends its creation record `cr` and its
`chain` instead: the chain is checked from `ik` (as `PUT /api/v1/me/p2p_identity/{ik}` checks
it), the proof is a signature by the primary key of one of its heads, the deepest records
that count, and the token names that head in a `head: {n, d}` claim. A chain that holds two
resets or removals by one key beside each other is refused. Stateless: nothing is stored, and
a binding can't be revoked before it expires (clients ask for a new one every day while the
badge is on). Requires a bearer token; guests can't call it. Answers 404 while the `p2p`
switch of `GET /api/v1/settings` is off. Strict rate-limit bucket.
Bindings are rare requests: at most `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR` (20) an hour and
`RARE_REQUESTS_PER_DAY` (100) a day per account by default.

preview of recent messages. The password step is the same as for
`POST /api/v1/servers/{name}/join`. You get the card for a server without a password, a server you
are a member of, or (for guests) a server that a valid `X-Guest-Grant` unlocks. All other names
get the same `401 Password required` without `X-Invite-Password`, also when the server does not
exist. A wrong password or an unknown name gets `404 Server not found or wrong password`.

answers like a password-protected one unless you are a member, and under `nobody` a request
without `X-Invite-Password` gets that 404 for every name instead of the 401. A server that
people who aren't members may read by its name always gets its card: with status `readable`
when what you sent doesn't join it.
Banned viewers get the card (with counts) only after they prove access, and never a preview.
The preview has the last 3 top-level messages of the first text channel without permission
rules.

Signed-in users may call it, and guests when guest access is on. Invite and general rate-limit
buckets.

Changes the display name, avatar, banner color, profile description and/or appear-offline
preference; fields left out stay as they are. A new avatar, display name or description
emits `user_updated` to users who share a server or DM with the user; changing `appear_offline`
emits `presence_mode` to the user's own connections, and the user then shows as offline
(or online again) to others. Banner color changes emit no event. A `display_name` answers
404 while the `display_names` switch of `GET /api/v1/settings` is off, and then nothing
changes. Requires a bearer token. General rate-limit bucket.
A new `display_name` is a rare request: each account may try at most `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR`
(20) an hour and `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_DAY` (100) a day by default, taken or free; your own
username and the name you have don't count.

GIF or WebP file of at most

(`AVATAR_UPLOAD_MAX_MIB`), and at most 40 megapixels. The server turns the image as its
EXIF orientation says, keeps the square `x`, `y`, `size` (without them the centered largest
square), and stores it at 64, 128 and 512 pixels as PNG when it has transparency and as
JPEG otherwise. An animated GIF, WebP or PNG also keeps its animation, as animated GIFs of
128 and 512 pixels, while the `animated_profile_pictures` switch is on: the id then ends in
`-a`, and an animation past `AVATAR_ANIMATION_MAX_FRAMES` (250), `AVATAR_ANIMATION_MAX_SECS`
(20) or `AVATAR_ANIMATION_MAX_MEGAPIXELS` (400, over all frames) is refused with 413.

built-in avatar (`avatar_kind`) stays as it is and shows where pictures are not shown.

token and the `profile_pictures` switch. Strict rate-limit bucket.

post.description:
Schedules the deletion of the calling account for 14 days later and signs it out
everywhere: every session of the account is revoked, this one too, and its WebSocket
connections close. Until then the account stays as it is. Signing in again with the
password or a provider keeps the account; so does `DELETE /api/v1/me/delete` from a session
opened another way. After the 14 days the account, its messages, its direct messages and
the P2P backups and P2P identities this instance holds for it are deleted. Confirm with the
account password or words, a fresh confirmation from a linked provider, or a `phrase` proof
(purpose `delete_account`, empty context) over a challenge from
`POST /api/v1/auth/recovery/challenge`; `fresh_session` is refused. Password and phrase
tries share the pace of password changes. Some accounts can't be deleted this way; they get
one answer that does not say why. Requires a bearer token. Strict and general rate-limit
buckets.

Stores the body, a sealed blob (`application/octet-stream`) of at most `limits.p2p_backup_bytes`
bytes, as version `version` of the backup of the P2P identity `ik`. The first upload of an `ik`
is version 1 and each later one the latest number plus 1; a number is never reused, also after
its version or the whole backup was deleted. Another number answers 409 with the latest number
in `X-Backup-Version` (0 when the account never backed up this `ik`). An account keeps backups of at most 8 P2P identities: a first
upload for another answers 409. No re-auth. Versions leave only with time: besides those that
aged out, an upload drops only a version of the current UTC day that is neither that day's first
nor among the last 3. Refused with 413 when the version is over `limits.p2p_backup_bytes`
(`Backup too large`) or when the versions your account keeps over all its identities would pass
`limits.p2p_backup_total_bytes` (`Backup storage full`); a refusal removes nothing. Up to 3
uploads and backup downloads per account are read at once, counted with media uploads in the
instance's upload buffer; a body that sends nothing for 30 seconds or takes over 10 minutes is
dropped with 408. Answers 404 while the `p2p_backup` or `p2p` switch of `GET /api/v1/settings`
is off, when your account is being deleted, and when the instance keeps no P2P backups. Requires
a bearer token; guests can't call it. Strict and general rate-limit buckets.
Uploads are rare requests: at most `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR` (20) an hour and
`RARE_REQUESTS_PER_DAY` (100) a day per account by default, over all its identities. An upload
refused by another limit or while the server is busy (429, 503) does not count.

record. Password and phrase tries share the pace of password changes: one every 3 seconds

post.description:
Stores one file for attaching to a message: send it as the first part of a
`multipart/form-data` body (any field name). The part's file name (default `file`) is kept
without path parts and control characters, cut to 255 bytes (keeping a short extension);
its content type (default `application/octet-stream`) is kept as `type/subtype` without
parameters when it is at most 127 bytes, else stored as `application/octet-stream`. Then
pass the returned `id` as
`media_id` when sending a message; only the uploader can attach it, and only to one
message. The file is deleted 24 hours after upload (attached or not), or at the time its
server chose when it is posted in a server (`upload_expiry` of the server); messages carrying
it then show it as removed (`media_removed` event). At most `limits.upload_bytes`
of `GET /api/v1/instance` per file, by default 25 MiB (`UPLOAD_MAX_MIB`), and
at most the instance's per-account budget (`UPLOAD_BUDGET_MIB`, 2 GiB unless set) of your
files at once. Each counts from its upload until it is removed, for at most 24 hours (files
your webhooks sent count too). Time a server adds with its `upload_expiry` counts against
that server and its owner instead (`kept` and `owner_kept` of
`GET /api/v1/servers/{name}/upload_expiry`).
At most 3 of your uploads are read at once. Each takes room for its whole declared body in
the instance's upload buffer (`UPLOAD_BUFFER_MIB`) before any of it is read, and together
they hold at most a quarter of it, three uploads (up to half of it) or one upload, whichever
is most. A body that sends nothing for 30 seconds, or takes over 10 minutes in all, is
dropped with 408.

With `place` naming the channel or DM the file will be posted in, a place that stores new

get.description:
Streams an uploaded file with its stored `Content-Type`, as an attachment
(`Content-Disposition: attachment`), with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a sandboxing
`Content-Security-Policy`. The token may come from the `Authorization` header or the
`rchat_token` cookie, so browsers can load it directly; guests may download when guest
access is on.

Every answer carries `Accept-Ranges: bytes`. One `Range` (`bytes=a-b`, `bytes=a-` or
`bytes=-n`) answers 206 with those bytes, `Content-Range` and their `Content-Length`; a range
that starts at or past the end answers 416 with `Content-Range: bytes */size`. Several ranges,
a header this server doesn't read, or an `If-Range` other than the file's `ETag` get the whole
file. With S3 storage a 206 holds at most 8 MiB from the range's start, and `Content-Range`
names the bytes sent. `HEAD` answers the same without the body.

Once attached, the file is visible to anyone who can read one of the messages carrying it,
with the same checks as listing messages: in a server without a password anyone not banned
from it, in a password-protected server its members or guests holding a grant for it (the
`X-Guest-Grant` header); in a channel with permission overrides (thread replies use their
channel) also the view permission, and without read-history access only messages posted since you
joined count; in a direct message its two participants. Before it is attached only the
uploader can fetch it. Access is checked before `If-None-Match`, so a 304 is only sent to
callers allowed to see the file. General rate-limit bucket.

post.description:
Deletes messages of one channel, thread or DM with the same rule as deleting one: your own
messages always; in server channels others' with the Manage messages permission in the
channel when you rank above their author; in DMs only your own. Requires a bearer token. With `ids` (at most 200) it deletes
now and answers what happened; unknown, unreadable and out-of-scope ids are counted as
`missing`, others' messages you may not delete as `others`. With `all: true` it starts a background job for every message
in the scope you can read and may delete (messages posted after the start are kept; on
Postgres a send still committing at the start can be included), minus `except` (at most 1000
ids), only between `after` and `before`, and only `author`'s when given. Send the dry run's
`upto` as `before: upto + 1` to delete only what it counted. A user runs at most one job
per scope (asking again answers the running job) and three at once. The job deletes in
batches of 200; `bulk_delete_progress` reaches your own connections after each batch, and
viewers get `messages_deleted` (ids only; viewers without read history of some of them get
only the ids they could read). Deleting a thread root also deletes all its replies, including
replies posted after the start. Deleting others' messages in a channel is audit logged with one
entry per request or job (`message.bulk_delete` with the count and the authors), which a job
writes with its first such batch and updates with every later one. `dry_run` counts without deleting. Deletes: 20 per minute;
dry runs: 60 per minute.

channel's Add reactions permission. In DMs, needs to be a participant. Only normal messages take reactions (not
call logs). A message has at most 20 different emojis. A repeated reaction changes nothing. A
new reaction emits `reaction_added` (`{server, channel_id, dm_id, dm_users, message_id,
thread_root_id, emoji, username, count}`, `count` = reactors of that emoji after the change)
to clients that can see the message. If the message is from someone else and the author can
still see it, the author gets one `ping` (kind `reaction`) per reactor and emoji. Removing and
adding the reaction again does not ping again. General rate-limit bucket.

is in the channel or DM of the root and has `thread_root_id` set. Requires a bearer token. In

the channel's Send messages permission, and the first reply of a thread also its Start threads
permission; a file also needs Attach files and a poll Create polls, and without Embed links the
reply gets no link previews. In a DM, it needs being a participant while neither blocked the
other, and DM text is not checked by the profanity filter. With slow mode, members without

(thread replies count). Emits `message` to clients in the server that can see the channel, or
to both DM participants. If the text has links, `embeds_resolved` follows when the previews are
fetched. Each `@username` outside code pings that user if they are a member who can see the
channel, or the other DM participant (at most 20 users, not yourself). The ping is stored for
`GET /api/v1/unreads` and sent as a `ping` event. `reply_to` can quote the root or another
reply of the thread. With `mention_reply` (default), its author gets a `reply` ping instead of
a mention ping. With `forward_of`, the reply is a copy of a message you can read (see
`SendReq`) and pings nobody. General rate-limit bucket.

post.description:
Stores the last-read message id of the caller for a scope (`c<channel id>` or `d<dm id>`). The
position only moves forward: a lower `last_read` changes nothing. The caller must be able to
read the scope. For a channel, the checks are the same as for listing its messages (not
banned, member of a password-protected server, view permission). For a DM, the caller must be
a participant. Otherwise nothing is stored. Also marks the unseen pings of the caller in the
scope as seen (all kinds, outside threads, ids up to `pings_until` if given). A thread scope
(`t<root id>`) stores no position. It marks pings on the replies of the thread as seen and has
the same checks as listing the thread. Requires a bearer token. If the position is stored or
pings were marked seen, emits `read_updated` to the connections of the caller with
`pings_until` (the highest ping id marked seen, 0 for none). Other devices then clear those
badges and keep newer ones. General rate-limit bucket.

switches of `GET /api/v1/settings` are off, are left out. The category `message` is opened
from a message and is not for a list of categories. The `ETag` changes whenever the answer
does: send it back as `If-None-Match` to get 304 without a body. Needs an account: guests

Reports a message, a member, an account or a server, or sends a bug report or feedback
(`target.kind` `none`). `to` says who gets it: `server` goes to the moderators of the server
it happened in (its members with Manage reports), `instance` to the instance. Messages in
direct conversations, accounts, servers and reports without a target go to the instance
only. `form` names the category of `GET /api/v1/report_forms` and `answers` answers its
fields after those of its base; without `form` the target picks `message`, `user` or
`server`. A report about a message keeps the message as it is now and, with `context`, up to
10 earlier messages you can read from the same place. Accounts, servers and messages that
answers name must be ones you can see. Limits per account and per `to`: the same account
(or any of its messages) once per 72 hours (`REPORT_SAME_TARGET_HOURS`), by default 3
different targets per day (`REPORT_TARGETS_PER_DAY`) and 10 reports per week
(`REPORT_MAX_PER_WEEK`); reports without a target count apart, by default 10 per week
(`REPORT_FEEDBACK_PER_WEEK`). Emits `reports_changed` to those who handle the report.
A server whose `members_visible` is off shows its members only to its members and instance
staff: anyone else gets `Not found` for a member of it, whatever the name. A 404 counts as a
miss (`LOOKUP_MISSES_PER_HOUR`, as for
`GET /api/v1/users/{username}/card`). Needs an account: guests get 401. Strict rate-limit
bucket.

get.description:
Searches channel messages (including thread replies; DMs are never searched), newest
first, with link previews. Signed-in callers search the servers they are members of,
skipping channels they cannot view and, without read-history access, messages from before
they joined. Guests (allowed when guest access is on) search only the servers listed in
`servers`, only channels without permission overrides, and only servers without a password
or with a valid grant in `X-Guest-Grant` (invalid grants are ignored). Messages by accounts
being deleted are left out. Each search that runs counts as one message search of the
caller, an account or the client address of a guest: 30 a minute with 10 at once
(`MESSAGE_SEARCH_PER_MINUTE`), one running at a time (`MESSAGE_SEARCH_AT_ONCE`; the next one
waits up to 5 s for it, and a newer one takes the place of one that waits), and for all
callers together as many at a time as `MESSAGE_SEARCH_CONCURRENT_LIMIT` allows (by default
half the connections reads use; a search waits up to 2 s for a place shared with former-member lists). A search refused
after its wait or replaced by a newer one does not count. General rate-limit bucket.

parameters.description:
Text the message content must contain, case-insensitive substring match after trimming.
Omit or leave blank to match every message. Must not contain NUL.

parameters.description: Only search this server (name, case-insensitive). Must not contain NUL.

parameters.description: Only search this channel id.

parameters.description: Only messages by this username (case-insensitive). Must not contain NUL.

`file` keeps only messages with an attachment; any other value is ignored. Must not

Legacy: skip this many results, capped at 500. Ignored when `cursor` is given. Prefer
`cursor`.

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `X-Next-Cursor` header. A blank value is ignored.

Guests only (ignored for signed-in callers, who search every server they are a member
of): the servers to search, as repeated parameters (`servers=a&servers=b`). Names are

Creates a server owned by the caller: they become its creator and an admin with all
permissions, and it starts with one text channel named `general`. Requires a bearer token.
The other fields choose how people join (`join`: by its name, with an invite, with a
password, or nobody new), whether search lists it, whether people who aren't members can read
it, a voice channel, the join and leave notices and how long uploads stay; without them anyone
joins the server by its name, or with its password when `password` is set. An `invite` or
`closed` server gets a random key of 10 characters (`name` in the answer) and
keeps it when it is renamed; its display name may be the name of other servers.
The instance may limit who creates servers (`server_creation` in `GET /api/v1/settings`):
accounts it leaves out get 404, and `can_create_servers` in `GET /api/v1/me` says which
applies to the caller. Emits `server_created` to the creator. Strict and general rate-limit
buckets.
New servers are rare requests: at most `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR` (20) an hour and
`RARE_REQUESTS_PER_DAY` (100) a day per account by default. A request refused while the server
is busy does not count.

patch.description:
Renames the server, switches it between public and password protected or changes how people
join it (`join`), sets, changes or clears its permanent password, changes its header colors,
and sets whether people who aren't members can read it (`public_read`) and see its members
(`members_visible`), whether members without moderation rights see the member list
(`hide_members`), whether search lists it (`listed`), and whether guests can participate
in text and voice (`guest_chat_opt_in`, `guest_voice_opt_in`); every field is optional.
Turning a guest choice on requires its site switch. A suspended choice can be kept or turned
off. A server people join with an invite or that is closed keeps its key when it is renamed,
so its passwords and links keep working; one that turns to `name` or `password` takes its
lowercase name as its key. Joining by password or by name with `protected` and `password`
sets the matching `join_mode`.
Requires the Manage server settings permission; `members: remove` together with `password` also
requires Kick. The built-in rchat server can't be given a password and keeps its key
`rchat` (a new name changes only its display name); its colors, `public_read`,
`members_visible`, `hide_members` and the guest participation opt-ins may change.

When `password` is present, `members: remove` removes every other member you could kick
(their roles are dropped, as if kicked; see `ServerDetail.roles_order_confirmed`) and existing
guest grants are revoked unless `keep_guests` is true with `members: keep`. The response
carries `removed` and `kept` counts. Making the server public, or changing its lowercase
name, revokes every extra password (extra password lookups are bound to the name, and invite
links carry it); revoked passwords stay listed until they are purged.

Emits `server_renamed` (with `old_name`) to the server when the name or display name changed,
otherwise `server_updated` with the new state (password flag, colors, description and icon), and
`members_purged` to the server and the removed members. Voice users who can no longer open
the server leave their call, and with `guest_voice: false` every guest in its voice gets
`voice_ended` (`Guests can't use voice in this server`). Strict and general rate-limit buckets.
A new `name` counts with the name checks of `GET /api/v1/servers/{name}/available`, and a new
`password` with new server passwords, as rare requests: at most `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR` (20) an
hour and `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_DAY` (100) a day per account and kind by default. A password refused
by its checks, or while the server is busy, does not count.

parameters.name: name

post.description:
Bans `username` from the server: they are removed with their roles dropped, taken out of the
server's voice channels, and blocked from rejoining until unbanned. Works on non-members too.
`duration_secs` (60 seconds to two years) ends the ban by itself; without it the ban holds
until someone lifts it. `reason` (at most 300 characters) is kept with the ban and in the
audit log. `purge_hours` (0 to 168) also deletes the messages the user sent in that many
hours before now, in the background: one bulk delete job of yours per channel and thread,
only where you may delete that user's messages. `purge_skipped` and `purge_busy` count the
places left alone.
Banning someone already banned replaces the ban's end and reason. Requires the Kick server
permission, and you must rank above the target as for a kick. Banning a
member posts a `leave` system message like leaving does (no reason shown). Emits
`member_kicked` (with `banned: true`) to the server and the user when they were a member,
otherwise `server_banned` to the user. A name with no account is banned like an account that
is not a member (the same answer), so it applies if the name is ever taken. A ban of someone
who is not a member, with or without an account, counts as a miss (`LOOKUP_MISSES_PER_HOUR`,
as for `GET /api/v1/users/{username}/card`); past the misses such bans are refused until the
hour ends. General rate-limit bucket.

post.description:
Checks the password of a password-protected server and returns a guest grant. Guests send the
grant in the `X-Guest-Grant` header to view the server without an account; it expires after
`GUEST_GRANT_DAYS` days without use (30 by default) and is revoked when the password changes
(unless the change kept guests). Each password has at most 2000 live grants by default
(`GUEST_GRANTS_PER_PASSWORD`; the permanent password counts as one), and at most 50 of them
per network by default (`GUEST_GRANTS_PER_NETWORK`; an IPv4 /24 or IPv6 /48); past that no
new grant is given until older ones expire. The API drives the
password step: without `password` every
name that is not a server without a password gets the same `401 Password required`, and a
wrong password or a name that does not exist gets the same `404 Server not found or wrong
password` (the password is always hashed, also for names that do not exist). Anyone may call
it, guests only when guest access is on. A server that people who aren't members may read
by its name answers `grant: null` under every joining rule, and any `password` is ignored.
For every other name the instance's `server_joining` applies as for
`POST /api/v1/servers/{name}/join`: under `invites` a server without a password answers
like a password-protected one, and under `nobody` every call gets the 404. Strict and
general rate-limit buckets.

Try again later` (JSON) when the password already has its live guest grants (by default 2000, `GUEST_GRANTS_PER_PASSWORD`), or your network has its share (by default 50, `GUEST_GRANTS_PER_NETWORK`). Returns users who sent a message or joined a voice channel in the server but are not members
now (for example former members), most recent interaction first, as pages of `limit` (default
and max 50). Only channel managers get this activity order. Other callers get only users with
a message the caller may read, newest such message first. Page with `cursor` from the
`X-Next-Cursor` response header (or the legacy `offset`); a cursor works only for the caller
it was given to.

Signed-in users may call it, and guests when guest access is on. Banned users get 403. On a
password-protected server signed-in callers must be members and guests need a valid
`X-Guest-Grant`; everyone else gets the same 404 as for a server that does not exist. A
server whose `members_visible` is off lists them only to its members and instance staff:

Returns members as pages of `limit` (default and max 50): online members first, then offline
ones, each alphabetical by username. Page with `cursor` from the `X-Next-Cursor` response header
(or the legacy `offset`). With `q` (username prefix) and/or `admins=1` it returns matching
members alphabetically, paged by `cursor` only. With `role` and `top_hoisted=1`, or with
`unhoisted=1`, it returns the members of one group of the member list (see `Role.hoist`)
alphabetically, paged by `cursor` only. With `q` and `suggest=1` it returns the
members `GET /api/v1/servers/{name}/mentions` suggests (mention autocomplete). With
`usernames` it returns just those users that are members, alphabetical and unpaged.

password-protected server signed-in callers must be members and guests need a valid
`X-Guest-Grant`; everyone else gets the same 404 as for a server that does not exist. A
server whose `members_visible` is off lists its members only to its members and instance
staff: everyone else gets an empty list in every mode.

The member list itself needs the site's `member_lists` switch on, the server's
`hide_members` off and View members (34359738368) held, in `channel_id` when given; members
with Manage server, Manage roles or Kick and ban, and instance staff, get it regardless of the
server and its permissions. Without it the caller gets 403, `suggest` an empty list, and
`usernames` only the members who wrote a message the caller can read, all shown offline.
Each call takes one of the caller's `list` lookups (`LOOKUP_LIST_PER_MINUTE`, 120 a minute
by default), or with `suggest` one of its `typeahead` lookups
(`LOOKUP_TYPEAHEAD_PER_MINUTE`, 300 a minute), counted per account, or per client address
without one. General rate-limit bucket.

post.description:
The instance will POST the chosen events of this server to the URL as signed JSON
(`X-Webhook-Signature`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`, `X-Webhook-Event`, `X-Webhook-Delivery`,
User-Agent `rchat-webhooks/1.0`). You are its owner: payloads include only channels you can
view, under your read-history rules, checked when each event happens and again at every
try; it turns off if you leave the server. A delivery is tried 6 times by default
(`WEBHOOK_ATTEMPTS`) with backoff (10 s to 30 min); redirects are not followed; after 10
failed deliveries in a row the webhook turns off. Only while the instance allows outgoing
webhooks. At most 10 per server by default (`SERVER_OUTGOING_WEBHOOKS_MAX`). Returns the
signing secret once. Logged in the audit log (host only). Strict rate-limit bucket.
New webhooks, new webhook tokens and secrets, and test events are rare requests of one kind: at
most `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR` (20) an hour and `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_DAY` (100) a day per account
by default.

It can expire (`expires_in` or `expires_at`, a temporary password) and can be limited to a
number of uses (`max_uses`, a ticket): every join and every guest grant through it uses one,
invite previews do not. A blank `password` generates four random words. The response is the
only time the password is returned. A chosen password needs at least 8 characters. A server
has at most 50 live extra passwords and keeps at most 500 in all (dead ones are purged 30
days after they stop working). Requires the Manage invites permission. Not available on the
rchat server. Strict and general rate-limit buckets.
New server passwords (also a new permanent one through `PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`) are rare
requests of one kind: at most `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR` (20) an hour and `RARE_REQUESTS_PER_DAY`
(100) a day per account by default. A password refused by its checks, or while the server is
busy, does not count.

timeout. While timed out they can read but not send, reply, forward into the server, edit,
react, start or reply in threads, pin or unpin, vote, type, or join voice channels; when they
are in a voice channel they are muted there until the timeout ends. DMs are not affected.

and you must rank above the member, or while the role order is unconfirmed their server
permissions must be a strict subset of yours (see `ServerDetail.roles_order_confirmed`). So
you can't time out yourself, the owner or admins above you. Logged in the audit log as `member.timeout`. Emits
`member_timeout` to the member and to members who hold Timeout members, and `voice_muted`
when they are in voice. General rate-limit bucket.

get.description:
How long files uploaded in the server stay, what that means for new files under the
instance's cap, and the kept space. `kept` is the bytes of the files the server keeps longer
than the instance default (`limits.media_retention_secs`), against the instance's limit for
one server (`UPLOAD_SERVER_KEPT_MIB`, 8 GiB unless set, 0 for none). `owner_kept` is the
same for all servers whose longer choice the same account is charged for, against the limit
for one account (`UPLOAD_OWNER_KEPT_MIB`, 16 GiB unless set, 0 for none). The account
charged is whoever set the longer choice or lengthened it last; only that account reads its
`bytes`, others with the permission read whether it is full, and nobody is told who it is.
Members read the choice in the server detail, and whether such limits exist in
`limits.upload_kept_limited` of `GET /api/v1/instance`. Requires the Manage server settings
permission. General rate-limit bucket.

put.description:
Chooses how long files uploaded in the server stay: the instance default, a custom time
(`seconds`, 3600 to 31536000) or `never` (kept until removed). While the instance has a cap
(`upload_expiry_max_days` in `GET /api/v1/settings`, 0 for none), `never` and longer times are
refused; a choice saved before the cap was lowered is shortened to it. Applies to files
already posted in the server too: their messages get the new expiry time, and files past it
are removed by the next sweep. Files in DMs keep the instance default.

A time longer than the instance default counts against the server's kept space (`kept`) and
against the space of one account across servers (`owner_kept`), not against the people who
uploaded the files. That account is you when you set a longer time where none was set, or
lengthen it; shortening it leaves the account as it was, and the default or a shorter time
charges nobody. The files the server keeps already follow the new time. The others are
extended newest first until one does not fit either space, and the rest stay for the
instance default; `extended` says how many of each. Nothing is removed for room, and a
later upload that does not fit is not refused: it stays for the instance default. Only the
site operator changes the limits (`UPLOAD_SERVER_KEPT_MIB`, `UPLOAD_OWNER_KEPT_MIB`).

Requires the Manage server settings permission. Emits `upload_expiry_changed` to the server's
members, who load the server again. General rate-limit bucket.

caller's `search` lookups (`LOOKUP_SEARCH_PER_MINUTE`, 30 a minute by default, shared with

get.description:
Returns what the caller may see of an account. `profile` (description, banner color and account
creation time) is set when the caller proves a relationship with the account: it is the caller's
own, they are friends, the account sent the caller a friend request, the account wrote in a
direct conversation with the caller, both are members of one server, the account is a member of
the server named with `server` and the caller may view that server (a member, anyone for a
server anyone can read (`public_read` in `PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`, `public_reading` in
`GET /api/v1/settings`), a guest with a valid `X-Guest-Grant`), or the caller sends a P2P
binding of the account in `X-Subject-Binding`. A guest that names no server is also shown
members of the servers its grants open. Through a server whose `members_visible` is off,
only its own members see its members' profiles. The instance's `profile_visibility` in `GET
/api/v1/settings` widens this to members of servers anyone can read (`public_servers`) or to
every account (`everyone`). An account's own choice (`profile` in `PATCH
/api/v1/me/privacy`) may narrow it to friends or widen it to everyone, as far as the
instance's `profile_choices` lets it.

`member` is the account's membership in `server`, set when the caller may view that server
and its member list (see `GET /api/v1/servers/{name}/members`) and the account is a member,
whoever may see the profile. An account with neither part
answers the same 404 as a name with no account, after the same checks. Works without a
token for guests when guest access is on.

Each call takes one of the caller's `profile` lookups (`LOOKUP_PROFILE_PER_MINUTE`, 120 a
minute by default), counted per account, or per client address without one. A caller that
used up its misses for the hour (`LOOKUP_MISSES_PER_HOUR`, 200 by default) gets the same 429
for every name until the hour ends. The 404s of this endpoint, of `POST /api/v1/blocks` and
of `GET /api/v1/users/{username}/profile` where this endpoint answers 404 too are misses, and
so are blocks of accounts whose card the caller may not see and bans of people outside the
server. General rate-limit bucket.

post.description:
Posts a message into the webhook's channel as the webhook. No bearer token: the URL is the
secret. Send JSON (at most 2 MiB), or `multipart/form-data` with the JSON in a `payload_json`
part (at most 2 MiB) and one file part (only while file uploads are on and the webhook has an
owner; at most `limits.upload_bytes` of `GET /api/v1/instance`, by default 25 MiB
(`UPLOAD_MAX_MIB`)). A multipart body takes room for its whole declared length in the
owner's share of the upload buffer before it is read, like the owner's own uploads. When the
webhook can not upload, or a body not declared over 2 MiB and 64 KiB finds no room free at
once, the body may be at most 2 MiB and 64 KiB and a file part in it is refused. A body that
sends nothing for 30 seconds, or takes over 10 minutes in all, is dropped with 408. Files
count against the upload budget of the webhook's owner, and the webhooks of one server
together get one more budget of the same size, each file for at most 24 hours like any
upload. The same rules as a
user's message apply: length limit, profanity filter, slow mode (per webhook, no exemption),
attachment switches, and reply and thread placement inside its channel. The webhook can
always send in its own channel and nowhere else; timeouts and blocks do not apply to it.
`@username` mentions ping as usual unless `allowed_mentions` narrows them; `@everyone`,
`@here` and roles ping only when `allowed_mentions` asks and the webhook's creator had
and still has the Mention everyone permission (mentionable roles also when asked). Rate
limits: by default 5 per 2 seconds per webhook (`WEBHOOK_HOOK_BURST`), 30 per minute per
channel (`WEBHOOK_CHANNEL_PER_MINUTE`), and the webhook bucket per IP. Wrong ids, wrong
tokens and deleted webhooks all get the same 404.

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket carrying JSON text frames, each an object tagged by `type` in
snake_case. The first frame must be `{"type": "auth", "token": "<token>"}`; leave out
`token` (or send an unknown one) to connect as a guest, which only works while guest access
is on, otherwise the socket closes. Any other first frame also connects as a guest.

A signed-in user is online in every server they are a member of while any of their
connections is open, unless they appear offline. They go offline about 10 seconds after
their last connection closes, so a quick reconnect shows nothing. Switching to appear
offline hides them at once; coming back online is allowed a few times in a row, then
about once per 10 seconds (the last setting wins). An account keeps at most 20
connections open by default: opening another closes the oldest with code 4008. Opening
them too often closes the new one with code 4029 (try again later). Then the client sends
`viewing` (the open
server, for its `presence_snapshot` and `presence_changed` events), `subscribe` (servers to
follow, with guest grants for password-protected ones), `voice_join` (optional `muted` and
`deafened`: what the joiner says about its own mic and sound) / `voice_leave`, `voice_audio`
(`{muted, deafened}` for the voice seat the connection holds, ignored without one; paced per
account, a few per second, the latest waits and wins), `call_start` (with `p2p` and `video` flags) / `call_accept` / `call_decline` / `call_leave`
for DM calls, `rtc_signal` for
WebRTC signalling, and `p2p_hosting` / `p2p_who` / `p2p_peer` for P2P files (`p2p_peer`
gives a reader of one message the hoster's peer id and a short-lived download token; `p2p_who`
never carries peer ids). `call_start` / `call_accept` for P2P calls and `p2p_hosting` (per
file id) may declare `relays`: up to 4 relay hosts (no port, no credentials) the sender's
side connects through; only the other side of that call or download gets them, in
`call_state.relays` and `p2p_peer.relays`. `typing` / `typing_stop` with a `scope` (`c{channel}`,
`t{root}` or `d{dm}`) show or clear a typing indicator where the sender may send messages
(others are ignored silently); the client repeats `typing` every few seconds while typing.
Others there get `typing` (`{scope, username, display_name, until}`, `until` in unix
seconds, 0 when stopped), routed like messages and never to the typer's own connections.
Guests are read-only: no presence, typing or calls. A guest connection first gets
`guest_name` (`{name}`): its name in voice rooms, `@guest:` and 16 hex digits, new for each
connection. A guest may join the voice channels it can view in the servers it follows
(`subscribe`), say its `voice_audio` there and send `rtc_signal` to the others in its room. While the instance's `calls`
setting is off, `voice_join`, and `call_start` and `call_accept` for a call that is not
P2P, get an `error` frame with reason `off_site` and control `calls`, and running voice
rooms and calls end (`voice_ended` with `Calls were turned off`, `call_state` ended); P2P
calls follow `p2p` the same way. The server sends the events in `WsEvent` (`apps/server/src/ws/event.rs`),
for example `message`, `message_updated`, `message_deleted`, `member_joined`, `presence_changed`,
`voice_state` (in the snapshot a connection gets on opening or subscribing, `audio` lists
each user in the room not at the default with `{username, muted, deafened}`), `voice_audio`
(`{server, channel_id, username, muted, deafened}`, one change), `call_state` (with `kind` and `video`; an active P2P call also carries its id
and the peer id of both tabs), `p2p_hosted` (tells a `p2p_hosting` sender which of its files are still live
attachments, and the key it checks download tokens with), `p2p_peer`, `error` (`{message}`, plus the `reason` object of REST errors when the error has one) and `resync` (fetch state again after missed events). Frames
are at most 64 KiB. The token goes in the `auth` frame, not in the bearer security scheme.
General rate-limit bucket for the upgrade request.

503.description: `Realtime is busy, try again in a moment` (JSON, reason `capacity`, control `ws_sockets_max`, `Retry-After: 5`): this copy holds `WS_SOCKETS_MAX` connections. Or `Realtime bus not ready` (plain text). Also `Server busy, try again in a moment`: the database did not answer in time. Retry after the seconds in the `Retry-After` header

get.description:
The signaling protocol of the `peer` package (1.0.2), for PeerJS clients: peer-to-peer
messages, files and calls find each other through it and then talk directly. Only when the
instance serves PeerJS signaling itself (`PEERJS_BUILTIN`); `peerjs_url` of
`GET /api/v1/instance` names the address. No authentication. While the `p2p` and
`p2p_attachments` switches of `GET /api/v1/settings` are both off, it answers 404 and closes
the connections that are open.

Frames are JSON text objects tagged by `type`. After the upgrade the server sends `OPEN`, or
refuses and closes: `ID-TAKEN` when a connected peer holds the id under another token (the
same token takes the connection over), or `ERROR` with `payload.msg` for a missing `id`,
`token` or `key`, a wrong key, an id or token over 128 bytes, or more peers than
`PEERJS_CONCURRENT_LIMIT`. A client sends `HEARTBEAT` (every 5 seconds; a connection silent
for 90 seconds is closed) and `OFFER`, `ANSWER`, `CANDIDATE` or `LEAVE` with `dst` and
`payload`; the peer `dst` gets the same frame with `src` set to the sender. Only the
connection that holds an id relays under it.

A frame for a peer that is not connected waits up to 5 seconds for it; after that the sender
gets `EXPIRE` with `src` set to that peer. A frame is refused the same way, at once, when
no room is left for it: 64 frames or 256 KiB wait for one absent peer, 512 KiB from one
client address, 8 MiB in all; 256 frames or 256 KiB are queued for one connection that reads
slowly, 2 MiB for the connections of one client address, 64 MiB in all; or the sender passes
its pace (1000 frames at once, then 100 per second). A frame of up to 16 KiB always fits
while less than 16 KiB is queued for its connection, so one that reads promptly keeps
getting small frames. A client address is the one the rate limits use (an IPv6 /64 counts as
one; forwarded headers count only from trusted proxies). A connection that does not take a
queued frame within 15 seconds is closed, and its id stays with its token for a minute. A
sender whose peer's connection just ended gets `LEAVE` from it. Frames are at most 64 KiB.
Peers of one process see each other; run one process, or keep the separate PeerJS server.

token.description:

optional `nonce`.

Who the assertion is for, usually the origin of the other instance; 1 to 512 bytes
after trimming. Becomes the JWT `aud` claim.

claim. Omit it when there is none.

action.description:
Dotted action name; the part before the dot is its group. `member`: `join` (with an
extra password or invite link: the target is that password by its id and label, never
its code; `kind` in the details is `password`, `link` or `standing`), `kick`, `ban`,
`unban`, `timeout`, `untimeout`, `profile_name` (a member's own server name),
`profile_reset` and `profile_unlock` (of a member's server profile), `voice_disconnect`,
`voice_mute`, `voice_unmute` (of a guest in voice), `admin_grant`, `admin_revoke`, `admin_transfer`, `admin_perms`. `role`: `create`,
`update`, `delete`, `assign`, `unassign`, `reorder` (`roles` in the details names up to
20 roles that changed place, `more_roles` counts the rest), `order_confirm` (the role
order now decides who may moderate whom), `order_init` (the instance ranked the roles of
a server that had no order; `ranked` is their number). `channel`: `create`, `update` (name, topic, slow
mode, restrictions), `delete`, `perm_set`, `perm_clear`, `reorder`, `category_create`,
`category_update`, `category_delete`, `separator_create`, `separator_update`,
`separator_delete` (the target is the separator by its id and label). `server`: `update`
(name and colors),
`system_messages`. `access`: `mode` (password protection and the permanent password, never
the password itself), `password_create`, `password_revoke`. `message`: `delete` and
`attachment_remove` (of other people's messages), `pin`, `unpin`, `poll_close` and
`poll_reopen` (of other people's polls). `report`: `status`, `assign`, `note`, `escalate`
(the target is the report's id, never a name; `channel` in the details is the channel
of the reported message), `mute` and `unmute` (of someone's reports to this server),
`export` (no target). Clients should show
unknown actions generically; new ones may be added.

not equal to the name of another channel in the server.

manage channels) can send. With no rules, only they can. Voice channels only accept
`false`.

3 or more newlines cut to 2. Checked by the profanity filter (`channel_topics` target).

ChannelPerm.description:
One permission rule on a channel. A member starts from what everyone holds in the server and
their roles add. The `everyone` rule applies first, then the channel's `restrict_view` and
`restrict_send` take View channels and the sending permissions away, then the rules of the
member's roles (an allow on any role wins over a deny on another), then the member's own rule.
Members with Manage channels keep every permission everyone can hold, and admins keep their
moderation permissions. Without View channels a member holds nothing in the channel. A role
rule that denies something only holds while the member keeps the role: leaving the server
drops every role, so a member can lose a deny by leaving and rejoining.

allow.description:
Permission bits the rule allows: 2 Manage messages, 32 Mention everyone, 131072 View
channels, 262144 Send messages, 524288 Read history, 1048576 Add reactions, 2097152 Attach
files, 4194304 Embed links, 8388608 Create polls, 16777216 Start threads, 33554432 Connect,
67108864 Speak, 134217728 Video, 536870912 Pin messages and 1073741824 Bypass slow mode.
A rule stored with the three flags alone reports the bits they stand for: `can_send`
covers Send messages, Add reactions, Attach files, Embed links, Create polls and Start
threads.

can_read_history.description: The subject can read messages sent before now.

can_send.description: The subject can send messages in the channel.

can_view.description: The subject can see the channel. Without it the other flags grant nothing.

mode.description:
How a `u:` rule combines with the member's roles. A `u:` rule stored with the three
flags alone is `merge`.

subject.description:
Who the rule applies to: `everyone`, `u:<username>` for a user or `r:<role id>` for a
role.

ChannelPermSet.description:
Request body for setting a channel permission rule: `subject` with either `allow` and `deny`
(and `mode`), or the three `can_` flags, or a rule as listed with its flags changed.

allow.description: Permission bits the rule allows in the channel (see `ChannelPerm.allow`).

can_read_history.description: The subject can read messages sent before now.

can_send.description: The subject can send messages in the channel.

can_view.description: With `can_send` and `can_read_history`: the subject can see the channel.

deny.description: Permission bits the rule denies in the channel. No bit may be in both masks.

oneOf.description:
How a `u:` rule combines with the member's roles. Defaults to the rule's current mode,
or `override` for a new rule. Only `u:` rules may be `merge`.

subject.description: Who the rule applies to: `everyone`, `u:<username>` or `r:<role id>`.

Choice.description: One option of a choice field.

id.description: 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and `_`, unique in its field. This is what an answer carries.

label.description: The text shown, up to 80 characters.

ConfigControl.description:
One control in the config view: its stored value, what the server config said at the last
start that set it, whether the stored value says the same, and whether the config pins it.

config.description: What the server configuration said at the last start that set it.

env.description: The name of the control in the server configuration.

key.description: The name of the control in the settings.

pinned.description: Whether the server configuration pins it, so it can not be changed here.

same.description: Whether the stored value says the same as the server configuration.

ConfigLimit.description: One limit in the config view. Limits change only in the server config, at a start.

default.description: The default; null when the limit is off by default.

env.description: The name of the limit in the server configuration.

range.description: The range it takes, as `low-high`; empty when any value is taken.

value.description: The value in use; null when the limit is off.

ConfigShare.description: A config share link of the signed-in user.

created_at.description: When it was created, Unix seconds.

expires_at.description: When it stops working, Unix seconds.

id.description: Link id, 12 random base62 characters; the link is `/config/{id}/`.

Confirmation.description: One-use Settings confirmation bound to the session returned by this exchange.

code.description: One-use fresh IdP proof for the newly issued bearer.

ConnectionBudget.description: What the Postgres connection limit leaves for more copies of this process.

used.description: Client connections open now, this process's included.

ConsentAction.description: What to do with an outstanding client login.

ConsentRequest.description: A client login receipt and the decision on it.

action.description: Describe the login, allow it, or cancel it.

receipt.description: Receipt from the consent return of the sign-in.

ConsentResult.description: An outstanding client login, with its sign-in code once allowed.

challenge.description: S256 challenge the client started the sign-in with.

code.description: Single-use sign-in code, present only after allow.

origin.description: Web origin that asked for the login.

CopiesReq.description: What the admin route that confirms the copies takes.

confirmed.description: Whether every copy of this site runs this build.

CreateChannelReq.description: Request body for creating a channel.

category_id.description:
Category to list the channel under, at its end. Optional; omitted or `null` lists it
at the end of the channels without a category.

oneOf.description: Channel kind, `text` or `voice`. Optional; omitted or `null` creates a text channel.

name.description:
Channel name. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; must not be blank, at most 100
characters, must pass the channel-name profanity filter and must not equal the name of
another channel in the server (exact, case-sensitive comparison).

restrict_view.description:
Create the channel with `restrict_view` on, so only people who manage channels see it
until rules are added. Optional; omitted means off.

text_only.description: Start a text channel with text-only messages.

answers.description: The answers to the form's fields after those of its base.

context.description: For a message: how many earlier messages to include, 0 to 10.

form.description:
The category id from `GET /api/v1/report_forms`. Left out, the target decides: `message`,
`user` (members and accounts) or `server`.

note.description:
A note, up to 1,000 characters. When the form has a text field `details` without an
answer, the note is its answer.

reason.description:
The reason: an option id of the form's `reason` field (by default `spam`, `harassment`,
`hate`, `sexual`, `violence`, `illegal`, `impersonation`, `other`). An id the form
doesn't offer counts as `other`. Left out for a form of base `none`, whose reason is the
answer to the field it marks.

name.description:
Server name. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed and the result becomes the
`display_name`; its lowercase form becomes the `name` used in URLs. Must not be blank,
at most 100 characters, not `.` or `..`, must pass the server-name profanity filter and
must not be taken by another server (case-insensitive).

password.description:
Optional join password. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; omitted, `null` or blank
creates a server without a password. Only for `join: password`.

CreateServerReq.description: Request body for creating a server.

CreatedAccount.description: A new account with its temporary password, which is in this answer only.

expires_at.description: When it stops signing in (unix seconds); null for never.

servers.description: What became of each server of the request.

allOf.description: The new password's details (its fields appear at the top level).

oneOf.description: For a link, its code and its path; `null` for a password.

password.description: The password itself; for a link, its code.

CreatedPassword.description:
A newly created extra password, with the password itself. This is the only time the
password is returned.

allOf.description: The server (its fields appear at the top level).

oneOf.description:
The invite link of a new `invite` server, unless `standing_link` was `false`; `null`
otherwise.

CreatedServer.description: A new server, with its invite link.

DatabasePool.description: A connection pool of this process.

oneOf.description: What the Postgres connection limit leaves; null on SQLite.

light_commits.description: How light writes commit, `sync` or `async`; null on SQLite.

online_indexes.description: The indexes built while the server runs; empty on SQLite.

oneOf.description: The read pool, when it is a separate one.

schema_version.description: The schema version stored in the database.

statement_timeout_secs.description: The statement timeout; null on SQLite.

DeleteAccount.description: The confirmation of an account deletion.

DeletionPending.description: An account that waits to be deleted.

delete_at.description: When the account is deleted (Unix seconds).

Delivery.description: One delivery: status codes and timings only, never response bodies.

created_at.description: When the event was queued, Unix seconds.

finished_at.description: When it was delivered or gave up, Unix seconds; `null` while `pending`.

last_code.description: HTTP status of the last try; `null` when it did not get a response.

last_error.description: Why the last try failed (plain ASCII), e.g. `Address not allowed` or `timed out`.

next_at.description: When the next try is due, while `pending`.

Direction.description: What a job does to the stored messages of its place.

DmCreation.description:
Who may start a direct conversation with `POST /api/v1/dms`: `everyone`, `friends` (only
with a friend) or `nobody`. Conversations that exist keep working, and so does the self DM.

DmPolicy.description: Who may open a DM with you or write in one.

DmSummary.description: A direct-message conversation of the signed-in user.

closed.description:
You closed it, so it is hidden from your DM list. Only `GET /api/v1/dms?ids=` returns
closed DMs; a new message in it or opening it again reopens it.

friend.description:
Whether the other person is an accepted friend; `false` for the conversation with
yourself.

is_self.description: Whether this is the conversation with yourself.

last_message_at.description: When the newest message or call log was sent, Unix seconds; `null` without messages.

last_message_id.description: Id of the newest message or call log; `null` without messages.

other.description: The other participant; the signed-in user for the conversation with yourself.

seal.description:
Whether new messages of the DM are stored encrypted with a key this site keeps (this is
not end-to-end encryption), and whether the site requires it. Set with
`PUT /api/v1/dms/{id}/seal`.

content.description:
The new text, at most `limits.message_chars` characters (Unicode code points; by default
4000, `MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS`). It may only be blank when
the message has an attachment.

media_alt.description:
New description of the attached image (see `media_alt` of `POST /api/v1/channels/{id}/messages`);
`null` or blank removes it, omit to keep it. Needs an attachment.
media_alt.example: A cat asleep on a red mat

Embed.description:
A link preview built from a page's OpenGraph, Twitter card or `<title>` metadata. Up to 3
per message, fetched after the message is sent when link previews are on.

banner_removed.description: The preview image was removed; the text part stays.

description.description: Page description, at most 600 characters, or `null`.

image_url.description:
Path on this instance that serves the preview image
(`/api/messages/{id}/embeds/{ord}/image?v=...`), or `null` when there is none or it was
removed. The instance fetches the image itself; the page's image host is never named.

ord.description: Position of the link among the message's previewed links, from 0.

site_name.description: Site name, at most 200 characters, or `null` if the page has none.

title.description: Page title, at most 300 characters, or `null`.

EmbedField.description: A field of a rich embed.

inline.description: Shown next to other inline fields. Defaults to `false`.

name.description: At most 256 characters, not blank.

EmbedFooter.description: The footer of a rich embed.

note.description: A note for the instance, up to 1,000 characters.

EveryonePerms.description: What everyone in a server may do.

EveryoneReq.description: Request body for changing what everyone in a server may do.

mask.description:
The bits this request changes. Bits outside it keep their current value. Defaults to
every bit everyone may hold.

ExchangeReq.description: Proof of possession for a returned sign-in code.

code.description: Single-use sign-in code received by the client.

confirm_as.description: Saved local username, required only when start requested confirmation.

username.description: Chosen local username when retrying a username selection.

oneOf.description: A session is ready for the verified account.
Fresh Settings proof when explicitly requested at sign-in.

end_session.description: Whether this provider supports configured sign-out.

token.description: Bearer token for the signed-in account.

oneOf.description: A local account name is required to finish this exchange.

reason.description: Reason for selecting a username, either taken or invalid.

oneOf.description: A provider identity has been attached to an existing local account.

provider.description: Configured provider ID of the linked identity.

ExchangeResp.description: Result of exchanging a verifier-bound sign-in code.

ExecuteReq.description: A message posted through a webhook. It needs `content`, an embed, a file or a poll.

oneOf.description: Which mentions may ping; see `AllowedMentions`.

avatar.description: Avatar for this message only: `identicon` or `#rrggbb`.

content.description:
Text, at most `limits.message_chars` characters (by default 4000,
`MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS`), like a user message.

oneOf.description: A poll, as for `POST /api/v1/channels/{id}/messages`.

reply_to.description: Quote this message (a user or poll message in the same channel, or thread).

thread_id.description: Post as a reply in the thread of this top-level message of the webhook's channel.

username.description: Name for this message only, 1 to 80 characters, checked like the webhook's name.

ExpiryMode.description: How a server keeps uploaded files.

Extended.description: What a change of the upload expiry did to the files already posted in the server.

files.description: Files that now stay longer than the instance default and did not before.

left_files.description:
Files left at the instance default because the kept space of the server or of the
account charged for its choice is full.

Features.description: Optional features and whether they are on right now.

backup_phrase.description:
Backup phrases (`/api/v1/me/recovery` and `POST /api/v1/auth/recovery`) are supported.
Whether new phrases can be set is the `backup_phrase` switch of `GET /api/v1/settings`.

guests.description: Guest access (reading servers without an account) is on.

p2p_attachments.description: Peer-to-peer attachments are on. With `uploads` also off, messages are text only.

p2p_backup.description:
P2P backups (`/api/v1/me/p2p_backup`) are kept, up to `limits.p2p_backup_bytes` per version.
Whether new ones can be uploaded is the `p2p_backup` switch of `GET /api/v1/settings`.

reports.description:
`POST /api/v1/reports` is available. Whether reports can be sent to servers and to the
instance are the `server_reports` and `instance_reports` switches of
`GET /api/v1/settings`.

Feed.description: The announcements visible to the caller at the time of the request.

announcements.description: Active banners in display order, excluding those dismissed by the account.

next_change.description: Earliest scheduled visibility change in Unix seconds, or null if none is pending.
