server_time.description: Server clock in Unix seconds when visibility was evaluated.

Field.description: One field of a report form.

help.description: A line under the label, up to 200 characters.

id.description: 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and `_`, unique in its form.

kind.description: How it is asked and answered.

label.description: The text shown, up to 80 characters. For a `checkbox` it is the statement.

max.description:
Text fields: the most characters (`short_text` 1 to 200, the default 200; `long_text` 1
to 2,000, the default 2,000). `multiple_choice`: the most options an answer picks.

min.description: `multiple_choice`: the fewest options an answer picks.

placeholder.description: Text fields: the hint shown while empty, up to 200 characters.

reason.description:
`single_choice` in a form of base `none`: its answer is the report's reason. At most one
field per form, and it offers the option `other`: an answer it doesn't offer counts as
`other`.

required.description: Whether a report needs an answer to it.

template.description:
`long_text`: the text the field starts with, up to 2,000 characters. An answer equal to
it counts as no answer.

FieldKind.description: How a field of a report form is asked and answered.

enabled.description: Whether people can send it. `GET /api/v1/report_forms` lists only forms that are on.

fields.description: Its fields in order, 12 at most: the fields of its base first.

id.description:
1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and `_`. `user`, `bug`, `server`, `general` and `message` always
exist.

label.description: Its name in the list and the form's title, up to 80 characters.

line.description: The line under its name in the list, up to 200 characters.

Format.description: The file format of an export.

ForwardRef.description:
The original of a forwarded message. The copy never changes when the original is edited or
deleted.

oneOf.description:
Who wrote the original; `null` once that account is deleted or banned (shown as a
deleted user). The copy itself stays.

created_at.description: Unix seconds when the original was sent.

dropped.description:
File name of an attachment of the original that was not forwarded: a peer-to-peer
attachment, or a file that already travels in 50 messages.

origin.description:
Where it came from, as a label: `Direct message`, `#channel - Server` when forwarded
inside the same server, or the server's display name when that server had no password
or when its sender chose to show it. `null` otherwise (a password-protected server's name
never leaves it unless its sender chose to show it). Kept for older clients; use
`origin_dm`, `origin_channel`, `origin_server` and `origin_server_channel`. Fixed at
forward time: later renames or password changes do not update it.

origin_channel.description:
Name of the channel it came from, without `#`, when forwarded inside the same server
and everyone there may see that channel; `null` otherwise.

origin_channel_id.description: Stable ID when the origin channel is public within the destination server.

origin_dm.description: Whether it came from a direct message.

origin_sensitive.description: The channel named by `origin_channel_id` carries the shared sensitive-content label.

origin_server.description:
Display name of the server it came from, when forwarded inside the same server, when
that server had no password or when its sender chose to show it; `null` otherwise.

source_id.description:
Id of the forwarded message. `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/location` tells where it is, if you
can read it.

online.description: Whether they have the site open (never for users who appear offline).

since.description: When you became friends, Unix seconds.

FriendReq.description: The user to send a friend request to.

username.description: Username, case-insensitive; a leading `@` is ignored.

created_at.description: When the request was sent, Unix seconds.

incoming.description: `true` when the request was sent to you.

user.description: The other user: the sender of an incoming request, the recipient of an outgoing one.

pings.description: Unseen friend pings (requests and accepted requests).

pings_until.description: Highest unseen friend ping id; 0 when there is none.

GroupBy.description: What a list of report groups sorts the reports by.

GroupMention.description: An `@everyone`, `@here` or role mention that pinged.

GroupPing.description: An unread message that pings the reader through group mentions.

kinds.description:
Its group mentions that address the reader (`role` once, however many of their roles it
names).

GuestAccessReq.description: Request body for getting guest access to a password-protected server.

password.description:
The server password. Omitted or blank answers `401 Password required` for every name
that is not a public server.

GuestGrant.description: A guest grant for a password-protected server.

grant.description:
Opaque grant token. Guests send it in the `X-Guest-Grant` header (comma-separated with
other grants) to view this server. It expires after `GUEST_GRANT_DAYS` days without use
(an instance setting, 30 by default) and is revoked when the server password changes, unless
the change kept guests. `null` for a server without a password: guests view it without a
grant.

GuestText.description: Ordinary guest text in a server channel.

content.description: Non-blank message text, subject to the instance message limit and filter.

thread_root_id.description: Optional top-level message whose thread receives this reply.

Head.description: A record of a key chain.

d.description:
Its identity: the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON without its signatures, base64url without
padding (43 characters).

n.description: Its number: 0 for the creation record.

Ice.description:
ICE servers for peer-to-peer connections (calls, P2P files). The instance never adds
servers on its own: public STUN, the built-in relay and extra servers are all opt-in.

relay.description: The instance runs its own relay (STUN, and TURN when `turn` is on).

stun.description:
STUN URLs anyone may use: the chosen public STUN servers, the built-in relay's STUN
address and STUN entries the operator added.

turn.description:
TURN relaying is available: signed-in users get short-lived credentials from
`GET /api/v1/p2p/ice`.

IceServer.description: One ICE server, as in the WebRTC `RTCIceServer` dictionary.

IceServers.description: ICE servers with short-lived TURN credentials.

expires_at.description:
Unix seconds when the built-in relay's TURN credentials expire, one hour after issue.
Fetch new ones before then.

ice_servers.description:
Pass these as `iceServers` of an `RTCPeerConnection`. STUN entries come first, then
the built-in relay's TURN entry with credentials, then the operator's TURN servers.

IconKind.description: How a server's icon is drawn, on the server's `banner_color` when it has one.

reauth.description:
How you confirm it: the password or words, or a `phrase` proof with purpose `p2p-data`
and the `ik` as context. `fresh_session` is refused.

chain.description: Every chain record of the identity, in any order.

cr.description: The creation record of the identity `ik`.

oneOf.description:
Needed only to replace the stored record with one that lacks some of it: the password or
words, or a `phrase` proof with purpose `p2p-data` and the `ik` as context.
`fresh_session` is refused. Checked whenever it is given.

IdentityRecord.description:
The public record of a P2P identity made with a backup phrase: its creation record and its
chain.

chain.description:
The chain records `{v, ik, n, prev, pk, keep, at, sig}` (a reset also `rk` and
`sig_next`, a removal `rk: ""`), each once, in order of `n`.

cr.description: The creation record `{v, ik, n, rk, pk, at, sig_ik, sig_rk}`, as it was sent.

ik.description: The P2P identity key: an Ed25519 public key, base64url without padding (43 characters).

IdpCode.description: A fresh sign-in with an identity provider.

code.description: The one-time RChat code delivered to `/sso` after the provider confirms the user.

actor.description: Who caused it: the author of the message, the user who reacted, or the friend.

channel_name.description: Channel name of a channel item.

content.description:
The start of the message text as written (at most 200 characters, a spoiler cut open
is closed again); clients mask markdown and spoilers. `null` for friend items.

created_at.description: When it happened, Unix seconds.

group_kinds.description: For a group mention, every way it addresses you (`everyone`, `here`, `role`).

id.description: Ping id, message id (`group`) or friend ping id; unique within `source`.

media_filename.description: File name of the message's attachment, if it has one.

media_spoiler.description: The attachment is marked as a spoiler.

message_id.description: The message (for reactions, your message that was reacted to).

role.description: The role name of a `role` mention (the first of your roles it names).

scope.description: `c<channel id>` or `d<dm id>`; `null` for friend items.

thread_root_id.description: Thread root when the message is a thread reply.

unread.description:
Not seen yet: an unseen ping, or a group mention newer than your read position in the
channel that you did not mark seen.

InboxKind.description: What an inbox item is about.

next.description: Cursor for the next page; `null` on the last page.

oneOf.description:
Bounds for `POST /api/v1/inbox/read_all`, read with the first page (no `cursor`); `null`
on later pages.

InboxReadAll.description: Mark every unread item up to `until` read, optionally only those a filter lists.

oneOf.description: Only this kind.

server.description: Only items in channels of this server.

InboxSource.description:
Where an inbox item comes from. Items of different sources are ordered by time; ids are
only unique within a source.

InboxUntil.description:
The newest id of each source when the page was read; send it back to mark all read, so
newer notifications stay unread.

friends.description: Id of the newest friend ping the inbox lists; 0 when it lists none.

groups.description:
Id of the newest message with a group mention the reader could be shown (sent since they
joined, in a text channel they can view); 0 when there is none.

pings.description: Id of the newest ping the inbox lists; 0 when it lists none.

IndexStatus.description: An index the server builds while it runs.

name.description: The index name.

percent.description: How far the build is, when it runs.

InstanceAuditEntry.description: One entry of the instance audit log.

action.description: What was done, for example `user.create` or `branding.change`.

actor.description:
Who did it; null for the server configuration, the command line, or an account deleted
since.

detail.description: More about the action; its fields depend on the action.

id.description: The entry id; newer entries have higher ids.

target.description: What it was done to: a username, a server, a setting.

InstanceInfo.description:
Who this instance is and where its services live. URLs come from `PUBLIC_URL` and the
related settings when set, otherwise from the request's host (forwarded headers count only
from trusted proxies).

api_url.description:
Root URL of the REST API. `<api_url>/v1` is version 1; the root itself uses the latest
version.

api_versions.description:
API versions this instance serves, each under `/api/<version>`; `/api/...` without one uses
the latest. Instances from before API versions leave this out and serve only `/api/...`.

auth.description: Live sign-in policy and public labels for configured providers.

e2ee.description:
Whether this build supports end-to-end encryption. The `e2ee` switch of
`GET /api/v1/settings` says whether it is on.

features.description: Optional features and whether they are on.

host.description:
Host (with port when not the default) users of this instance belong to, as in
`user@host`.

ice.description:
ICE servers for peer-to-peer connections. Empty and off unless the operator enables
them.

id.description: Random id generated once per instance and kept in its database.

instance_url.description: URL of this document on this instance (`GET /api/instance`, the latest version).

jwks_uri.description: URL of the instance's JSON Web Key Set.

mark_url.description: URL of the instance's mark, a 192 by 192 PNG, when it uploaded one.

name.description: Display name of the instance (`instance_name` of `GET /api/v1/brand`, default `RChat`).

peerjs_url.description:
PeerJS signalling server used for peer-to-peer file sharing and calls: `/peerjs` of this
origin, unless the operator names another address (`PUBLIC_PEERJS_URL`) or the port of a
separate PeerJS server on this host (`PEERJS_PORT`). Left out while the instance has
both `p2p` and `p2p_attachments` off: it runs no signalling then.

public_url.description: Origin of the web app, without a trailing slash.

sfu.description:
The instance runs its media server for calls (`SFU_ENABLED`, off by default). The `sfu`
switch of `GET /api/v1/settings` says whether calls use it.

widgets.description:
Whether this build supports embeddable widgets. The `widgets` switch of
`GET /api/v1/settings` says whether they are on.

ws_url.description:
WebSocket gateway URL on the latest version; `/api/v1/ws` in place of `/api/ws` is
version 1.

Invite.description: An invite card for a server.

password_expires_at.description:
When the extra password that unlocked this card expires, Unix seconds. `null` unless an
extra password with an expiry unlocked it.

password_uses_left.description:
Uses left on the extra password that unlocked this card. `null` unless an extra
password with a use limit unlocked it.

preview.description:
The last 3 top-level messages of `preview_channel`. Empty when the viewer is banned or
there is no preview channel.

preview_channel.description:
Name of the channel the preview comes from: the first text channel without any
permission rules. `null` when the viewer is banned or no such channel exists.

preview_channel_id.description: Stable identifier of the authorized preview channel.

preview_sensitive.description: The shared viewing label of the authorized preview channel.

status.description: The viewer's relation to the server.

InviteLinkInfo.description: An invite link: its code and the path of the link on this instance.

code.description: The code. It is the whole link: whoever has it can join while it works.

path.description: The path of the link on this instance, `/i/{code}/`.

InviteStatus.description:
The viewer's relation to an invited server: `member` (already a member), `banned` (banned
from the server), `joinable` (may join now: no password, or the invite password or a guest
grant was accepted) or `readable` (may read it, as anyone may, but what was shown doesn't
join it: joining needs a password or invite, or nobody new may join). Guests never get
`member` or `banned`.

IssuedPassword.description: A temporary password as it is returned once to whoever issued it.

expires_at.description: When it stops signing in (unix seconds); null for never.

JobStatus.description:
Where a bulk delete job is: `running`, `done`, `cancelled` (by you) or `failed` (the scope
went away or an error stopped it).

JoinMode.description:
How people join a server: `name` (anyone who knows its name), `invite` (only with an invite
link, or a password the managers made), `password` (its name and its password) or `closed`
(nobody new).

JoinReq.description: Optional request body for joining a server.

password.description:
The server password. Ignored for servers without a password and for servers you are
already a member of. Omitted or blank asks the API whether a password is needed: the
answer is `401 Password required` for every name that is not a public server.

JoinedVia.description: The extra server password a member joined with.

label.description: Its label; `null` when it has none.

KeptSpace.description:
The files a server keeps longer than the instance default (`limits.media_retention_secs`),
counted against the instance's limit for one server.

bytes.description: Bytes of the files the server keeps longer than the instance default.

full.description:
Whether a file of the largest upload size (or of the whole limit, if smaller) no longer
fits. A new file that does not fit is not refused: it stays for the instance default
instead, until space frees up.

limit.description: Most bytes one server may keep that way (`UPLOAD_SERVER_KEPT_MIB`); 0 for no limit.

LayoutCategory.description: A category in a channel layout, with its channels.

channels.description: Ids of the category's channels, top first.

name.description: Category name.

LayoutReq.description:
Request body for reordering a server's channel list. Together, `uncategorized` and the
`channels` of every category must list each channel of the server exactly once, and
`categories` must list each category exactly once.

categories.description: Categories, top first, with their channels.

separators.description:
Where each separator goes, every separator of the server exactly once, top first. Leave
it out to keep each separator in its list after as many channels as before.

uncategorized.description: Ids of channels without a category, top first.

version.description: The `layout_version` the order is based on.

Level.description:
Who may see an account's profile, least open first: `friends` (only an account's own
choice), `shared` (people who share a server, a direct conversation the account wrote in or
a friendship with it), `public_servers` (also everyone, for an account in a server anyone
can read) and `everyone`.

assertion_ttl_secs.description: Seconds an identity assertion stays valid.

avatar_upload_bytes.description: Largest profile picture upload, in bytes: by default 8 MiB (`AVATAR_UPLOAD_MAX_MIB`).

catch_up_delay_ms.description:
Most milliseconds a client waits at random before it reloads the open view after a
reconnect: by default 5000 (`CATCH_UP_DELAY_MS`).

media_retention_secs.description:
Seconds an uploaded file is kept before it is deleted, unless its server chose otherwise
(`upload_expiry` of the server). Files in DMs always use this.

message_chars.description: Longest message text, in characters: by default 4000 (`MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS`).

name_chars.description: Longest username, server, channel or role name, in characters.

p2p.description:
The P2P device limits this instance sets (`P2P_LIMITS`), by name (`local.` and a name of
the P2P limits registry), each inside its range. P2P devices start with them in place of
the defaults. Empty when it sets none.

p2p_backup_bytes.description:
Largest P2P backup version, in bytes: by default 64 MiB (`P2P_BACKUP_MAX_MIB`, at most
`UPLOAD_BUFFER_MIB`); 0 when the instance keeps no P2P backups.

p2p_backup_total_bytes.description:
Most bytes of P2P backup versions one account keeps over all its identities: by default
256 MiB (`P2P_BACKUP_TOTAL_MIB`); 0 for no total.

page_size.description: Default page size of list endpoints.

reconnect_base_ms.description:
Milliseconds before the first realtime reconnect, doubling with each try: by default
1000 (`RECONNECT_BASE_MS`). Clients wait a random time up to it.

reconnect_cap_ms.description: Most milliseconds between realtime reconnects: by default 30000 (`RECONNECT_CAP_MS`).

reconnect_floor_ms.description: Fewest milliseconds before a realtime reconnect: by default 250 (`RECONNECT_FLOOR_MS`).

resync_jitter_ms.description:
Most milliseconds a client waits at random before it reloads what it shows after the
server asked all clients to: by default 10000 (`RESYNC_JITTER_MS`).

scheduled_per_account.description:
Most scheduled messages one account can have waiting: by default 100
(`SCHEDULED_PER_ACCOUNT`); 0 for no cap.

servers_per_account.description:
Most servers one account can be in, creating included: by default 1000
(`SERVERS_PER_ACCOUNT`); 0 for no cap.

session_idle_secs.description:
Seconds a session lasts without a request the user made: by default no limit, 0
(`SESSION_IDLE_SECS`). Requests with an `X-Background: 1` header don't count.

session_max_age_secs.description: Seconds a session lasts after sign-in: by default no limit, 0 (`SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECS`).

upload_bytes.description: Largest upload, in bytes: by default 25 MiB (`UPLOAD_MAX_MIB`).

upload_kept_limited.description:
Whether the instance limits how much a server and one account keep longer than
`media_retention_secs` (`UPLOAD_SERVER_KEPT_MIB`, `UPLOAD_OWNER_KEPT_MIB`). While it
does, a file that does not fit is still posted and stays for `media_retention_secs`.

Link.description: A link the app shows with its about text and under the sign-in form.

LinkedProvider.description: An external sign-in method attached to this account.

can_unlink.description: Whether this provider can currently be removed while preserving usable sign-in methods.

linked_at.description: Unix time in seconds when this sign-in was linked.

name.description: Configured display name, falling back to the identifier.

expected.description: Optional destination from each link, keyed by message ID. A mismatched destination is omitted.

ids.description: Up to 50 message ids. Repeated ids count once.

oneOf.description: Routing fields only.
Routing fields and the message preview.

LocationResult.description: The readable destination, optionally including a preview of the message.

LoginReq.description: Login credentials. Give exactly one of `password` or `words`.

password.description: The text password. Omit when using `words`.

username.description:
Username, case-insensitive. A name that passes for exactly one account's username in
look-alike characters signs in to that account.

words.description:
The account's 7 words in the order they were chosen (case-insensitive). Omit when using
`password`.

LogoutForm.description: Signed notification from the configured identity provider.

LogoutResp.description: Result of ending the current local session.

end_session_url.description: Configured identity provider's sign-out URL, if enabled for this session.

Me.description: The signed-in user's own account, with the first page of their servers and DMs.

appear_offline.description: Whether the user chose to appear offline: others do not see them as online.

avatar_color.description:
Lowercase `#rrggbb` avatar color when `avatar_kind` is `color`. For identicons it is the
chosen background color, or null for the default background.

avatar_image.description: The id of the uploaded profile picture (see `UserRef.avatar_image`); null without one.

avatar_kind.description: Avatar style: a generated identicon or a solid color.

banner_color.description: Lowercase `#rrggbb` profile banner color; null means the default derived from the avatar.

bio.description: Profile description (at most 190 characters, may contain newlines); null when unset.

can_create_servers.description:
Whether this account may create servers (`server_creation` in `GET /api/v1/settings`
applied to it).

delete_at.description:
Set while the account waits to be deleted at its own request: when it is deleted (Unix
seconds). `DELETE /api/v1/me/delete` keeps the account. Absent for every other account.

display_name.description: The name shown for the user: the username as registered until they change it.

dms.description:
First page (up to 50) of the user's DM conversations: the self DM first, then by latest
message, newest first.

dms_cursor.description: `cursor` value for the next page of `GET /api/v1/dms`; null when there are no more.

dms_more.description: Whether more DMs follow; fetch them from `GET /api/v1/dms`.

has_password.description: Whether the account has a local password or sign-in words.

is_site_admin.description: Whether the account is the site administrator.

password_kind.description: How the account signs in: a text password or 7 words

oneOf.description:
Set while the account's password is a temporary one issued for it: when it stops
signing in, and whether this session must change it first. Null for every other
account.

servers.description: First page (up to 50) of the servers the user has joined, oldest join first.

servers_cursor.description: `cursor` value for the next page of `GET /api/v1/me/servers`; null when there are no more.

servers_more.description: Whether more joined servers follow; fetch them from `GET /api/v1/me/servers`.

username.description: Lowercase username, the account's unique key.

MePatch.description: Changes to the signed-in account. Every field is optional; omitted fields stay unchanged.

appear_offline.description: Appear offline to others (`true`) or show real presence again (`false`).

avatar_color.description:
`#rrggbb` color, stored lowercase. Required when `avatar_kind` is `color`. For
`identicon` it is the optional background color; omit it (or send `null`) for the
default background. Ignored when `avatar_kind` is omitted.

oneOf.description: New avatar style. Omit to keep the current avatar (and ignore `avatar_color`).

banner_color.description:
`#rrggbb` banner color, stored lowercase; `null` resets it to the default derived from
the avatar. Omit to keep it.

bio.description:
Profile description, at most 190 characters (code points) after cleanup: trimmed,
control characters other than newlines dropped, runs of 3 or more newlines cut to 2.
Empty or `null` clears it. Omit to keep it.

display_name.description:
The name shown for you, 1 to 32 characters after trimming, without control, format or
invisible characters, never passing for the instance staff or for another account's
username, and checked by the profanity filter (`usernames` target). Not unique, and never
used for mentions or sign-in. Omit to keep it.

appear_offline.description: Whether the user appears offline to others.

banner_color.description: Lowercase `#rrggbb` banner color; null means the default derived from the avatar.

bio.description: Profile description as stored after cleanup; null when unset.

MeUpdated.description: The signed-in user's public profile after an update, plus their own settings.

MediaKind.description:
`server`: uploaded through `POST /api/v1/media` and stored by the instance. `p2p`: kept in the
sender's browser and shared peer to peer while they are online; the server stores only the
metadata.

MediaRef.description: A file attached to a message, stored on the server or shared peer to peer.

alt.description:
A description of the image for people who can't see it, at most 1000 characters.
Absent without one.

expires_at.description:
Unix seconds when the file goes away (`null`: kept until removed). For `server` media
this follows the server's upload expiry (24 hours after upload by default; DMs always
use the default); for `p2p` media it is the sender's chosen expiry.

hoster.description: Username of the user sharing a `p2p` file; `null` for `server` media.

id.description:
32 hex characters. For `server` media, download it from `/api/v1/media/{id}`; for `p2p`
it is the id the hoster's browser shares the file under.

mime.description:
MIME type, known for `p2p` media; `null` for `server` media. Declared by the sender and
not verified: clients decide how to show a file from its bytes.

removed.description: The attachment is gone: it expired, or its author or a moderator removed it.

removed_by_author.description: The attachment was removed on purpose rather than expiring.

sha256.description:
SHA-256 of a `p2p` file (64 lowercase hex characters), computed by the sender when
attaching it, so recipients can check what the hoster serves. `null` for `server` media
and for files sent by clients that predate it (unverified).

size.description: Size in bytes; `null` when a `server` file is no longer stored.

spoiler.description: Clients blur the attachment until it is clicked.

allOf.description: The user, flattened into this object.

is_admin.description: Whether the member is a server admin.

is_creator.description: Whether the member created the server.

oneOf.description:
The extra password the member joined with. Only in `GET /api/v1/servers/{name}/members`
and `GET /api/v1/servers/{name}/members/search` for callers with the Manage invites
permission, and only for members who joined with an extra password that is still
listed; absent otherwise. It disappears once the password
row is purged, 30 days after the password was revoked, expired or used up.

online.description:
Whether the member is online right now: signed in with at least one open connection,
whatever server or page they have open. Members who chose to appear offline are always
`false`.

perms.description:
Admin permission bits (see `Role.perms`). For an admin, 0 means every permission and
any other value is the granted subset; always 0 for non-admins, whose permissions come
from their roles.

oneOf.description:
The name and avatar the member set for this server; absent when they use the account's,
and while server profiles are off.

role_ids.description: Ids of the server roles assigned to the member.

Member.description: A server member: the user's `UserRef` fields plus their standing in the server.

MemberFacts.description: A user's membership in the server asked for with `server`.

is_admin.description: Whether the user is a server admin.

is_creator.description: Whether the user created the server.

joined_at.description: When the user joined the server, Unix seconds.

online.description:
Whether the user currently shows as online in the server (false while they appear
offline).

perms.description:
Admin permission bits granted to the user as a server admin; 0 for non-admins. Role
permissions are in `roles`.

oneOf.description:
The name and avatar the user set for the server; absent when they use the account's,
and while server profiles are off.

role_ids.description: Ids of the roles assigned to the user, ascending.

roles.description: The roles assigned to the user, by id ascending.

oneOf.description:
The user's running timeout in the server. Only for viewers with the Timeout members
permission (kept while they are timed out themselves); absent otherwise and when none is
running.

allOf.description: The member, flattened into this object.

created_at.description:
When their account was made; `null` for an account that shows its profile only to its
friends.

MemberHit.description:
A member a search found: the member as member lists show them, with their join and
account times.

MemberLook.description:
The part of a server profile shown wherever the member is listed: each field is `null` when
the member uses the account's value.

avatar_color.description:
Lowercase `#rrggbb` color of a `color` avatar or background of an `identicon`. Only set
together with `avatar_kind`.

oneOf.description: How the avatar is drawn in this server; `null` uses the whole account avatar.

name.description: The name shown for the member in this server.

MemberSort.description: How a member search is ordered. Ties go by username, in the same direction.

MemberTimeout.description: A timeout that is running now.

remaining.description: Seconds left when the response or event was made.

until.description: When it ends, in unix seconds.

Message.description: A message in a channel, a direct-message conversation or a thread.

oneOf.description: Call details when `kind` is `call`; `null` otherwise.

channel_id.description: The channel it was sent in; `null` for direct messages.

content.description:
Text, at most `limits.message_chars` characters (by default 4000,
`MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS`); may be empty when there is an attachment, and is empty
for call logs.

created_at.description: Unix seconds when it was sent.

dm_id.description: The direct-message conversation it was sent in; `null` for channel messages.

edited_at.description: Unix seconds of the last edit; `null` if the message was never edited.

embeds.description:
Link previews; empty until they are fetched, then delivered by the `embeds_resolved`
WebSocket event and included in later reads.

oneOf.description:
For a forwarded message, where its content came from; `null` otherwise. The content,
attachment and link previews above are a copy made when it was forwarded.

group_mentions.description:
`@everyone`, `@here` and role mentions that pinged when the message was sent (the author
had the Mention everyone permission, or the role allows anyone to mention it). Only
top-level channel messages have them; edits never change them. Empty otherwise.

id.description: Message id, unique across the instance and increasing over time.

kind.description:
`user` for a normal message, `poll` for a poll (`poll`; `content` is the question),
`call` for a direct-message call log, `pin` when someone pinned a message
(`pin_message_id`; empty `content`), or `join` / `leave` when the author joined or left
the server (empty `content`; leaving includes kicks and bans).

oneOf.description: The attachment, or `null`.

no_previews.description: Suppress generated link cards for this message.

pin_message_id.description:
For a `pin` message (someone pinned a message), the id of the pinned message; `null`
once that message is deleted, when it was sent before you could read the channel's
history, and for other kinds.

pinned_at.description: Unix seconds when the message was pinned; `null` if it is not pinned.

oneOf.description:
For a `poll` message, the poll as you see it (counts only when you may see them; your
own vote only in message lists and `GET /api/v1/polls/{id}`). For a forwarded poll, a frozen
`snapshot` that takes no votes. `null` otherwise.

reactions.description:
Emoji reactions in the order they were first added, with `me` for the caller. Filled in
message lists; empty in WebSocket events (clients apply `reaction_added` and
`reaction_removed`).

reply_count.description: Number of thread replies to this message.

oneOf.description: For an inline reply, the message it quotes; `null` otherwise and in search results.

thread_root_id.description: For a thread reply, the id of the message the thread hangs off; `null` otherwise.

unreadable.description:
The stored message can't be opened: its encryption key is missing or the stored record
is damaged. `content` is empty then. Left out otherwise.

MessageLocation.description: Where a message is, as far as the caller can read it.

author.description: Who wrote it (for a pin notice, who pinned; for a call log, who called).

channel_id.description: The channel; `null` for a DM message.

content.description: First line of its text as plain text, like a reply quote (see `ReplyRef.content`).

created_at.description: Unix seconds.

dm_id.description: The DM conversation; `null` for a channel message.

oneOf.description: For a forwarded copy, its original as `Message.forward` describes it.

forwarded.description: It is a forwarded copy of another message.

kind.description: `user` for a normal message, `call` for a call log, `pin` for a pin notice.

server.description: Lowercase name of the message's server; `null` for a DM message.

thread_root_id.description: For a thread reply, the thread's root message; `null` otherwise.

MessagePlace.description: The destination of a readable message.

channel_id.description: Destination channel ID for a channel message.

dm_id.description: Destination conversation ID for a direct message.

server.description: Canonical server name for a channel message.

oneOf.description:
What a forward of this message with `show_source: true` would name: its server, and its
channel when everyone in that server may see it. `null` for a direct message and for a
server you read only through staff access, whose forwards keep the default naming.

thread_root_id.description: Root message ID for a thread reply.

MessageWebhook.description: The webhook part of a message.

embeds.description: Rich embeds it posted, in order.

id.description: Id of the webhook that posted it (it may have been deleted since).

ModAction.description: What was done about a resolved report.

Mode.description: Which audience may use the channel and whether it supports participation.

MutedReporter.description: An account whose reports are muted.

created_at.description: When it was muted, unix seconds.

display_name.description: 1 to 32 characters; the username as written when left out or blank.

servers.description: Up to 20 servers to join besides the default servers.

NewConfigShare.description: Request body for creating a config share link.

blob.description:
The encoded config string (`rc1.` followed by base64url), at most 16384 bytes. The server
stores it as is and never reads it.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the link expires: one of 600, 3600, 86400, 604800 or 2592000.

name.description: 1 to 80 characters.

url.description:
`https` URL (plain `http` only for hosts the operator allows), at most 2048 characters,
without credentials. Private, loopback and link-local addresses and the instance's own
are refused unless the operator allowlists the host.

NewPassword.description: Request body for creating an extra server password.

expires_at.description: When it expires, Unix seconds, at least 60 seconds and at most one year away.

expires_in.description:
Seconds until it expires, 60 to 31536000 (one year). Use either this or `expires_at`;
omit both for no expiry.

oneOf.description:
`password` (the default) or `link`: an invite link, a generated code (returned in
`password` and `link`) that people join with at `/i/{code}/`, found by the code alone.
A link takes no `password`.

label.description:
Label shown in the password list and in the member list ("Joined with"). Trimmed;
blank or omitted means none; at most 100 characters.

max_uses.description: How many joins and guest grants it allows, 1 to 10000; omit for unlimited.

password.description:
The password. Trimmed; blank or omitted generates four random words joined by `-`. At
most 200 characters, and different from the permanent password and from every other
password of the server (also dead ones that are still listed).

NewSeparatorReq.description: Request body for creating a separator.

category_id.description:
Category to list it at the end of; `null` or left out lists it at the end of the channels
without one.

label.description:
Text on the line, kept exactly as written after trimming surrounding whitespace: at most
100 characters, no control characters, and it must pass the category-name profanity
filter. Empty or left out: a bare line.

style.description: How the line is drawn; `dots` when left out.

oneOf.description: Defaults to `identicon`.

channel_id.description: A text channel of the server that you can see.

name.description: 1 to 80 characters. It cannot be the username or display name of anyone in the server.

open.description: The reports with the status `open` that you can see.

OpenCount.description: The open reports of one server.

open.description: Its reports with the status `open` that you can see.

OpenDmReq.description: The user to open a DM with.

username.description: Username, case-insensitive. Your own username opens your self DM.

count.description: How many ballots count for it.

OutgoingList.description: The outgoing webhooks of a server, and whether the instance sends them at all.

available.description: The instance switch; while off nothing is sent and new ones cannot be made.

OutgoingPatch.description:
Changes to an outgoing webhook; omitted fields stay. Turning it on clears the failure
count.

events.description: The new event list, at least one.

name.description: 1 to 80 characters.

url.description:
A new URL, checked like `NewOutgoing.url`. Required when the change makes you the
owner: the previous owner's URL is never shown to you.

secret.description:
HMAC-SHA256 key: `X-Webhook-Signature` is `sha256=` plus the hex HMAC of
`<X-Webhook-Timestamp>.<raw body>`.

OutgoingSecret.description:
An outgoing webhook with its signing secret, returned once when it is created or the
secret is reset.

OutgoingWebhook.description: An outgoing webhook. The signing secret is never listed.

created_at.description: When it was created, Unix seconds.

oneOf.description:
Its owner: who created it, or the last manager who changed its URL or events, turned it
on or reset its secret. `null` once that account is gone. Payloads include only what
this person can view when each try is sent, under their read-history rules.

disabled_at.description: When the instance turned it off, Unix seconds; `null` otherwise.

disabled_reason.description:
Why the instance turned it off: `failures` (10 failed deliveries in a row) or `owner`
(its owner is no longer a member). Turning it on again makes you the owner.

enabled.description:
Off when a manager turned it off, after 10 failed deliveries in a row, or when its owner
left the server.

name.description: Name shown to managers.

url.description:
Where events are POSTed. Only its owner gets the whole URL; other managers get its
scheme and host (`https://example.com/`), since the path can itself be a credential.

url_hidden.description: Whether `url` is cut to its scheme and host because you are not the owner.

OwnerKept.description:
The files kept longer than the instance default by all servers whose longer choice one
account is charged for, counted against the instance's limit for one account. The account
charged for a server is whoever set its longer choice or lengthened it last.

bytes.description:
Bytes of those files across the servers the account is charged for. `null` unless you
are that account.

full.description:
Whether a file of the largest upload size (or of the whole limit, if smaller) no longer
fits. A new file that does not fit is not refused: it stays for the instance default
instead, until space frees up.

limit.description:
Most bytes the servers charged to one account may keep that way together
(`UPLOAD_OWNER_KEPT_MIB`); 0 for no limit.

P2pAttachment.description:
A file offered peer to peer by the sender, who becomes its `hoster`. The server stores only
this metadata, never the file.

expires_in_seconds.description:
Optional lifetime in seconds from now, must be positive. The message's `expires_at`
becomes now plus this; omit for no expiry.

filename.description:
File name shown to recipients. In server channels it is checked by the profanity filter
when that is enabled for file names.

mime.description: MIME type as reported by the sender, not verified; at most 255 characters.

p2p_id.description: Transfer id chosen by the sender: exactly 32 hexadecimal characters.

size.description:
File size in bytes, from 0 to 2^53 - 1. There is no other size limit: the bytes never
reach the server.

oneOf.description: The account's current password or words.

keep_recovery.description: `false` also removes the account's backup phrase. Omit or `true` to keep it.

new.description: The new password or words. Either kind is allowed, regardless of the current one.

oneOf.description: Fresh provider code or signed backup phrase when setting the first password.

PasswordKind.description:
What an extra password is: `password` (typed, or four generated words), `link` (an invite
link: a generated code people join with at `/i/{code}/`) or `standing` (the server's own
invite link, which members share; see `GET /api/v1/servers/{name}/invite`).

PasswordMembers.description:
What happens to the other members when a server password is set, changed or cleared:
`keep` (default) keeps everyone; `remove` removes every other member the caller could kick
(see `ServerDetail.roles_order_confirmed`).

PasswordStatus.description: `live` passwords let new people join; `expired`, `used_up` and `revoked` ones no longer do.

PermMode.description: How a rule for one member combines with the rules of their roles.

PermSyncReq.description: Request body for syncing a channel's permission rules with its category's.

confirm.description:
Sync even when the category's rules let someone see or send in the channel who could not
before.

PermsReq.description: Request body for setting a server admin's permissions.

mask.description:
The permission bits `perms` sets; send 1610740735. The admin keeps the bits they hold
outside it. Set bits within 1023 are also added for compatibility. Defaults to 511.

perms.description:
Permission bitmask: 1 Manage channels, 2 Manage messages (delete messages of others and
close their polls), 4 Kick, 8 Delete server, 16 Manage admins, 32 Mention everyone and
roles, 64 View audit log, 128 Timeout members, 256 Manage webhooks, 512 Manage reports,
4096 Manage server settings, 8192 Manage invites, 16384 Manage roles, 32768 Assign roles,
65536 Reset server profiles, 536870912 Pin messages and 1073741824 Bypass slow mode. Bits
outside 1610740735 are dropped. For an admin, 0 means all permissions.

PhraseProof.description: A backup phrase signature over a recovery challenge.

nonce.description: The nonce from `POST /api/v1/auth/recovery/challenge` for this account.

sig.description:
The Ed25519 signature by the account key of the backup phrase over the challenge, as
base64url without padding (86 characters).

removed.description: Whether the account had a backup phrase.

Ping.description:
A notification for one user, delivered live as the `ping` WebSocket event. Unseen pings are
counted per scope in `GET /api/v1/unreads` and marked seen by `POST /api/v1/read`.

created_at.description: When the ping was created.

excerpt.description: Start of the message text, at most 200 characters.

message_id.description: The message that pinged, or that was reacted to; 0 in the `friends` scope.

scope.description:
`c<channel id>` (thread replies use their channel and set `thread_root_id`), `d<dm id>`,
or `friends` for friend requests and accepted requests.

server.description: Server of a channel scope; `null` for DMs.

thread_root_id.description:
Root message when the ping is about a thread reply. Thread pings count toward their
channel scope but are only marked seen by reading the thread (`t<root id>`).

Poll.description: A poll as one viewer sees it.

allow_add.description: Members who can vote may add options while it is open.

allow_change.description: Voters may change or take back their vote while it is open.

anonymous.description: Nobody can list who voted for what.

closed.description: No more votes: closed early or past the deadline.

closes_at.description: Unix seconds of the deadline; `null` without one.

kind.description: What kind of vote it takes.

max_choices.description: For `multiple` the most options a vote may pick; 1 for other kinds.

min_choices.description: For `multiple` the fewest options a vote must pick; 1 for other kinds.

mine.description:
The viewer's own vote: option ids (in rank order for `ranked`), or the score for
`rating`. `null` when they did not vote, and in WebSocket events.

oneOf.description: The counts, or `null` while they are hidden from this viewer (see `show_results`).

snapshot.description: A copy made when the poll was forwarded: it never changes and takes no votes.

PollKind.description: What kind of vote a poll takes.

emoji.description: The emoji shown before the text, or `null`.

id.description: Option id, used in votes and counts.

PollOptionReq.description: One option of a new poll.

emoji.description: Optional emoji shown before the text: one emoji of the Unicode emoji list.

text.description:
The option text, 1 to 100 characters after trimming. Options of one poll must differ
(ignoring case).

PollReq.description: A poll to post as a message (`SendReq.poll`). The message text is the question.

allow_add.description:
Members who can vote may add options (up to 20 in total) while the poll is open; only for
`single`, `multiple` and `ranked`. Defaults to `false`.

allow_change.description: Voters may change or take back their vote while the poll is open. Defaults to `true`.

anonymous.description:
Votes are anonymous: nobody can list who voted for what, and live updates go out in
5-second steps. This holds against API users; someone with the database and the password
pepper (unless `PASSWORD_PEPPER` is set outside it) could still link votes to accounts.
Defaults to `false`.

duration_seconds.description:
Close the poll this many seconds after posting, 60 to 2592000 (30 days). Omit for no
deadline.

kind.description: What kind of vote it takes.

max_choices.description:
For `multiple`: most options a vote may pick, `min_choices` to the number of options.
Defaults to the number of options.

min_choices.description: For `multiple`: fewest options a vote must pick, 1 to the number of options. Default 1.

options.description:
2 to 20 options for `single`, `multiple` and `ranked`; must be empty for `rating` and
`yes_no` (which get Yes, No and Abstain).

question.description: The question, 1 to 300 characters after trimming.

PollResults.description: Counts of a poll. Never includes who voted.

average.description: `rating` only: the average score; `null` without votes.

counts.description:
Ballots per option in option order: for `single`, `multiple` and `yes_no` the ballots
that picked it, for `ranked` the ballots that ranked it first. Empty for `rating`.

distribution.description: `rating` only: how many voters gave each score, from 1 to `scale`.

rounds.description: `ranked` only: the instant-runoff rounds, first to last.

winner.description:
`ranked`: the runoff winner. `single`, `multiple`, `yes_no`: the option with the most
votes when exactly one has the most. `null` without votes or on a tie.

voted_at.description: Unix seconds of their current vote.

Posted.description: A posted message and its server-scoped guest session.

message.description: The persisted message with its public guest author.

session.description: Private credential for this guest in this server. Keep it inside the client.

friend_requests.description: Who can send you friend requests.

profile.description: Who can see your profile and find you by name.

PrivacyPatch.description: Privacy settings to change; missing fields stay as they are.

oneOf.description: Who can DM you.
Who can send you friend requests.

Who can see your profile and find you by name: `default`, `friends`, `shared` or
`everyone`.

ProfanityTargets.description:
Where the profanity filter applies when `profanity_filter` is on. `links` covers the
domain part of URLs inside messages: off skips `scheme://host` and still reads the
path and the prose.

file_names.description: File names of attachments in server channels and threads.

links.description: The domain part of URLs inside messages.

messages.description: Message text in server channels and threads (not direct messages).

ProfanityTargetsPatch.description: The profanity filter targets to change. A target left out stays as it is.

category_names.description: Whether the filter checks category names.

channel_names.description: Whether the filter checks channel names.

channel_topics.description: Whether the filter checks channel topics.

file_names.description: Whether the filter checks file names.

role_names.description: Whether the filter checks role names.

server_names.description: Whether the filter checks server names.

banner_color.description: Lowercase `#rrggbb` banner color; null means the default derived from the avatar.

bio.description: Profile description, at most 190 characters, may contain newlines; null when unset.

created_at.description: When the account was created, Unix seconds.

oneOf.description:
Membership in the server given by `server`; null when `server` was omitted, the server
does not exist, the viewer may not view it, or the user is not a member.

server_banner.description: The `#rrggbb` banner color the user set for that server; absent like `server_bio`.

server_bio.description:
The description the user set for the server given by `server`; absent when they have
none there.

user.description: The user's public identity and avatar.

ProfileChoices.description:
What accounts may choose for themselves (`profile_choices`): `any` of the three choices,
only a `narrower` one than the instance's level (a wider one acts as no choice), or nothing
(`site`: every account follows the instance's level, and stored choices are kept).

ProfileFacts.description: The part of a card that an account shows only to people it has a relationship with.

banner_color.description: Lowercase `#rrggbb` banner color; null means the default derived from the avatar.

bio.description: Profile description, at most 190 characters, may contain newlines; null when unset.

created_at.description: When the account was created, Unix seconds.

server_banner.description: The `#rrggbb` banner color the account set for that server; absent like `server_bio`.

server_bio.description:
The description the account set for the server named with `server`; absent when it has
none there or is not shown as a member of it.

ProfileField.description: A part of a server profile a moderator can reset.

ProfileMember.description: A user's membership in the server asked for with `server`.

is_admin.description: Whether the user is a server admin.

is_creator.description: Whether the user created the server.

joined_at.description: When the user joined the server, Unix seconds.

online.description:
Whether the user currently shows as online in the server (false while they appear
offline).

perms.description:
Admin permission bits granted to the user as a server admin; 0 for non-admins. Role
permissions are in `roles`.

oneOf.description:
The name and avatar the user set for the server; absent when they use the account's,
and while server profiles are off.

role_ids.description: Ids of the roles assigned to the user, ascending.

roles.description: The roles assigned to the user, by id ascending.

oneOf.description:
The user's running timeout in the server. Only for viewers with the Timeout members
permission (kept while they are timed out themselves); absent otherwise and when none is
running.

ProfilePolicy.description:
Who can see your profile (your description, banner color and when you joined) and find you
by name. The instance's `profile_choices` decides which choices apply.

ProfileReset.description: Request body for resetting parts of a member's server profile.

fields.description: The parts that go back to the account's values. May be empty when `lock_secs` is sent.

lock_secs.description:
Locks the member's server profile against their own edits: 86400 (1 day), 604800
(7 days) or 2592000 (30 days) from now, or -1 until a moderator lifts the lock. Left out
or `null` keeps the lock as it is.

reason.description: Why, shown in the audit log; at most 300 characters.

ProfilesMode.description: What members of a server may set in their server profile.

ProviderInfo.description: An identity provider offered on the sign-in screen.

id.description: Identifier used in the OIDC start route.

name.description: Display name shown on the provider sign-in button.

encryption_ready.description:
Whether encrypted storage can be turned on here: `ready`; `first_need` (no key yet, the
first switch makes one); `keys` (`This site needs an encryption key first`); or
`updating` (`Not available while this site updates`).

encryption_required.description:
The site requires encrypted storage: every server and DM stores new messages encrypted,
and the app encrypts what it stores of P2P rooms and DMs on this device. Older servers
send nothing, which reads as off.

guest_servers.description:
Keys of the servers a guest starts in: the instance's default servers that people who
aren't members can read right now, in the instance's order. A default server that only
members read is never listed. Older servers send no list.

PublicSettings.description:
The public settings as `GET /api/v1/settings` and the `settings_changed` WebSocket event
send them: every switch of `Settings`, plus the lists that are public.

ReAuthBody.description: How you confirm a sensitive change. Give exactly one field.

fresh_session.description:
`true` to confirm with this session alone. No change accepts it: it answers 401
`Confirm with your password`.

oneOf.description: A single-use code from a fresh sign-in with the linked provider.

A backup phrase signature over a fresh challenge. The change says which purpose and
context it signs.

count.description: How many users reacted with it.

emoji.description:
The emoji, as sent by the reactors (skin tones included), for example U+1F44D (thumbs
up).

first_at.description: When the first of them reacted; reactions are listed in this order.

me.description: Whether the caller is one of them.

ReadBatchReq.description: Mark several channels, DMs and threads read.

scopes.description:
Up to 200 scopes: `c<channel id>`, `d<dm id>` or `t<thread root id>`. Repeated scopes
count once.

ReadReq.description: Mark a channel, DM or thread read up to a message.

last_read.description:
Id of the last message read. A value lower than the stored one leaves it unchanged.
Threads store no position (send 0 or the last reply id).

pings_until.description:
Highest ping id the client has shown for this scope: only pings up to it are marked
seen, so a ping that arrives meanwhile keeps its badge. Omitted: every unseen ping.

scope.description:
`c<channel id>`, `d<dm id>` or `t<thread root id>`: the letter followed by one or more
ASCII digits.

ReadState.description: The stored read position of a scope.

last_read.description: The stored last-read message id: the higher of the previous value and the request.

scope.description: The scope from the request, as given.

bus.description:
The realtime bus is healthy: always `true` without `REDIS_URL`; with it, this
instance is publishing to and following the Redis stream and has caught up.

db.description: The database answered a trivial query, or every connection of this copy is in use.

sockets.description: This copy takes new realtime connections: `false` while it holds `WS_SOCKETS_MAX`.

Reason.description:
Why a request was refused, for programs. An error without one is a denial about a server,
channel or message the caller can't open, an error that has no kind yet, or an answer of an
older server.

control.description:
The setting or limit that refused: a key of `GET /api/v1/settings`, or a limit's name
such as `upload_max_mib`. For `confirm`, what to confirm.

field.description: The name of the request value that is wrong.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again. The `Retry-After` header carries the same number.

until.description:
When (unix seconds) a lock ends; 9223372036854775807 for one that stays until a
moderator lifts it.

ReasonKind.description: What kind of error it is.

RecoverReq.description: A recovery sign-in: a backup phrase signature over a fresh challenge, and a new password.

new.description: The new password or words, with the rules of registration.

nonce.description: The nonce from `POST /api/v1/auth/recovery/challenge` for this username.

sig.description:
The Ed25519 signature by the account key of the backup phrase over the challenge, with
purpose `recover` and an empty context, as base64url without padding (86 characters).

username.description:
The username the challenge was issued for, case-insensitive. A name that passes for
exactly one account's username in look-alike characters recovers that account.

reauth.description:
The account password or words, fresh confirmation from a linked provider, or a `phrase` proof with purpose `remove` and
an empty context.

RecoverySet.description: A new backup phrase for the account.

key.description:
The account key of the new phrase: an Ed25519 public key as base64url without padding
(43 characters).

reauth.description:
The account password or words, fresh confirmation from a linked provider, or a `phrase` proof with
purpose `set` and the new `key` as context. `fresh_session` is refused.

RecoveryStatus.description: Whether the account has a backup phrase. The key itself is never returned.

fresh_session.description:
Whether this session may set a phrase with `fresh_session` alone. Always false.
A first phrase requires the account password or words, or fresh confirmation from a linked provider.

set_at.description: When it was set; null when none is set.

RegisterReq.description: A new account. Give exactly one of `password` or `words`.

avatar_color.description:
`#rrggbb` color, stored lowercase. Required when `avatar_kind` is `color`. For
`identicon` it is the optional background color; omit it for the default background.

password.description: A non-empty text password. Omit when using `words`.

username.description:
1 to 100 characters, not blank, without `@`, control, format or invisible characters,
variation selectors, spaces other than U+0020 or spaces at either end. Unique
case-insensitively and in look-alike characters: a name that passes for another account's
username or a banned one is refused. The given case becomes the display name. Checked by
the profanity filter (`usernames` target).

words.description:
Exactly 7 words picked from `GET /api/v1/auth/words/{username}` (case-insensitive). Their
order matters: logging in needs the same words in the same order. Omit when using
`password`.

Registration.description:
Who may create an account with a password: anyone (`open`), nobody because accounts come
from single sign-on (`sso`), or nobody (`closed`).

Relation.description: How you and another user are connected.

RelayStatus.description: The relay this instance advertises to P2P clients.

allocations.description: Open relay allocations, when this process runs the relay.

enabled.description: Whether the instance advertises a relay.

turn.description: Whether it relays media (TURN) and not only finds addresses (STUN).

healthy.description: Whether reads go to it now.

lag_ms.description: How far it is behind, when known.

ReplyRef.description: The message a reply quotes, as shown above the reply.

oneOf.description: Who wrote it; `null` when `deleted`.

content.description:
First line of its text as plain text (formatting removed), at most 200 characters; empty
when it has only an attachment or is `deleted`. Spoilers are wrapped in `||` (always
closed, also when cut off), and a literal pipe or backslash has a backslash before it, so
`||` only ever marks a spoiler.

deleted.description:
The quoted message was deleted or cannot be shown to you (sent before you joined and you
cannot read the channel's history). Only `id` and `mention` are set then.

oneOf.description: For a quoted forward, its original as `Message.forward` describes it.

forwarded.description: The quoted message is itself a forward (shown with a small "Forwarded" marker).

mention.description: The reply pinged the quoted message's author (`mention_reply`).

partial.description:
Only `id` and `mention` are set: WebSocket events never carry the quoted message.
Clients fill it from a loaded copy of the original or by reading the reply through the
message list (`around` = the reply's id).

answers.description:
The answers to the form's fields, in form order, with the labels they had when the
report was sent. Empty answers are left out.

events.description: The newest 50 lines of the history, oldest first.

events_cursor.description:
The cursor for the lines before `events`: pass it as `cursor` to
`GET /api/v1/reports/{id}/events`. `null` when `events` is the whole history.

franked.description: Whether the content is proven to be what was sent. Always `false` for now.

related.description: The 50 newest other reports about the same target that you can see.

report.description: The report as the list shows it.

snapshot.description: The reported content as it was when the report was sent.

ReportEvent.description: A line of a report's history.

oneOf.description: Who did it; `null` for `created` and for deleted accounts.

created_at.description: Unix seconds.

detail.description:
`status`: `{status, action?}`. `assign`: `{assignee}`. `note`: `{text}`. `escalate`:
`{note?, to}` on the report and `{note?, from}` on its copy.

ReportForms.description: The report forms of the instance.

forms.description: The categories in list order, 12 at most.

rev.description: Grows by one with every change of the forms.

ReportFormsReq.description:
Request body of `PUT /api/v1/admin/report_forms`: every category, in list order, and the
revision the editor loaded.

rev.description: The revision the editor loaded. One that is not the stored revision is refused with 409.

key.description: The group's key: pass it as `key` with the same `by` to list its reports.

label.description:
A name for the group, where the key is not one: a role, channel, server, reason or
category name, `Deleted user`, `Unassigned`, `No role`, `No channel` or `No server`.

open.description: Of those, the ones with the status `open`.

oneOf.description: The account the group is about, for `member`, `reporter` and `assignee`.

ReportPatch.description: Changes to a report. Left-out fields stay as they are.

oneOf.description:
What was done about it. Only together with `status: "resolved"`; any other status
clears it. `delete_server` and `ban_owner` are carried out by this request.

assignee.description:
Who handles it: a username, or `null` for nobody. For a server's report a member with
Manage reports who is not the one reported; otherwise yourself.

owner.description:
With `ban_owner`: the account to ban, the server's creator or one of its admins. Left
out, it is the creator.

oneOf.description: The new status. Any status can follow any other.
What was done, on a resolved report.
Who handles it.

channel.description: The channel's name now, or when the report was sent if it is gone.

channel_id.description: The channel of the reported message.

created_at.description: Unix seconds.

escalated.description: Whether it was passed on to the instance.

excerpt.description:
The first 200 characters of the reported message, the name of the reported account or
server, or the first text answer of a report without a target.

form.description: The category: the id of the form the report was sent with.

form_label.description: The name the category had when the report was sent.

reason.description:
The reason id. For a report without a target it is the answer to the field its form
marks as the reason, or `other`.

reason_label.description: The label the reason had when the report was sent.

oneOf.description: Who sent it; `null` once the account is deleted.

role.description: The name of the reported member's first role when the report was sent.

server_name.description: That server's display name when the report was sent.

oneOf.description: The reported account; `null` for webhooks, servers, deleted accounts and none.

target_key.description:
Groups the reports about the same target: `u:<username>` for an account and its
messages, `s:<server>` for a server, `d:<id>` once the account is deleted, `-` for
none.

webhook.description: The name of the webhook whose post was reported.

RequestOutcome.description: The answer to a friend request.

user.description: The user the request went to.

RequestPolicy.description: Who may send you a friend request.

RequestStatus.description: What sending a friend request did.

RequireReq.description: What the admin routes that require encryption take.

RequiredView.description: Whether the site requires encryption, and where that is set.

pinned.description: The server configuration sets it, so the admin page can't.

Resolved.description: How many reports a bulk change closed.

count.description: The reports that were open or in review and are closed now.

RichEmbed.description:
A simple rich embed posted by a webhook: a card with a title (optionally linked), text,
fields and a footer. All text counts toward 6000 characters per message, and passes the
profanity filter like message text. Nothing in it is fetched.

color.description: Accent color as an integer `0xRRGGBB` (0 to 16777215).

description.description: At most 4096 characters. Rendered like message text (markdown).

oneOf.description: Small text at the bottom.

url.description: An `http(s)` link for the title, at most 2048 characters.

RingStatus.description: What the admin page and `server keys status` show. It never holds key material.

backed_up_at.description: When the key copy was confirmed saved (unix seconds).

database_key.description: Whether the `secrets` purpose runs on the key kept in the database.

fingerprints.description: `id:fingerprint` of every root key, the wrapping key first.

kept.description:
`id:fingerprint` of the instance key file's keys kept to open older data keys while
`ENCRYPTION_KEYS` replaces them.

key_file.description: The path of the instance key file, when there is one.

kms.description: The key service's address and key, when one is set.

oneOf.description: Set when a start made relay or P2P secrets again.

color_names.description: The role colors the names of its members.

display_position.description:
Place in the order roles show in (the display order): a role shows at its display
position, or at its `position` when this is `null`, and roles at one place show in role
order. A member's name takes the color of the first role they hold in display order that
has `color_names`, and the icon of the first one with an icon.

hoist.description:
Members whose first role in display order with `hoist` is this one show in a group of
their own in the member list. Only the first 10 such roles in display order form groups.

icon.description:
One emoji shown after the names of its members (for example U+1F6E1 U+FE0F, shield), or
`null`.

id.description: Role id, unique across the instance.

mentionable.description:
Anyone who can send in a channel may mention the role with `@name`. Otherwise only members
with the Mention everyone permission can.

name.description: Role name, at most 100 characters.

perms.description:
Permission bits of the role: 1 Manage channels, 2 Manage messages (delete messages of
others and close their polls), 4 Kick (also bans), 8 Delete server, 16 Manage admins,
32 Mention everyone and roles (`@everyone`, `@here` and every role), 64 View audit log,
128 Timeout members, 256 Manage webhooks, 512 Manage reports (see and act on reports in the
server), 4096 Manage server settings, 8192 Manage invites, 16384 Manage roles, 32768 Assign
roles, 65536 Reset server profiles (clear and lock the server profile of another member),
536870912 Pin messages, 1073741824 Bypass slow mode.
A role can also hold the bits everyone can hold (see
`PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}/everyone`).

position.description:
Place in the server's role order: a higher position ranks higher, and between two roles
at one position the one with the lower id. A member ranks by the highest role they hold.

RoleDisplayFollowReq.description: Request body for showing roles in their role order again.

version.description: The `roles_version` of the order you looked at (see `ServerDetail.roles_version`).

RoleDisplayReq.description: Request body for setting the display order of roles.

order.description: Every role id of the server once, the one shown highest first.

version.description: The `roles_version` the order was made from (see `ServerDetail.roles_version`).

RoleLimits.description:
Roles the caller can't edit, delete or assign because of who holds them or of the channel
permission rules that name them. Every list is empty unless the caller has Manage roles or
Assign roles.

channel_denies.description:
Roles with a channel permission rule that denies something the channel gives everyone who
views it. Deleting one or taking it away from anyone, yourself included, would widen
access, so it needs Manage channels. Always empty when you have Manage channels.

channel_grants.description:
Roles whose channel permission rules allow something you don't hold in that channel. You
can't assign them. With Manage channels only the moderation permissions of a channel
(Manage messages, Mention everyone, Pin messages) can be missing.

held_above.description:
Roles you can't edit, delete, give or take away because they do not rank below your
highest role. While the role order is unconfirmed (`ServerDetail.roles_order_confirmed`),
also the roles held by another member whose server permissions are not a strict subset
of yours: you can't edit or delete those.

RoleOrder.description: The role order of a server.

order.description: Every role id of the server, the highest first.

version.description: The version of this order, for the next change.

RoleOrderConfirmReq.description: Request body for confirming the role order.

version.description: The `roles_version` of the order being confirmed (see `ServerDetail.roles_version`).

RoleOrderConfirmed.description: The answer to confirming the role order.

confirmed.description: Always `true`: the role order now decides who may moderate whom.

RoleOrderReq.description: Request body for a new role order.

order.description: Every role id of the server once, the highest first.

version.description: The `roles_version` the order was made from (see `ServerDetail.roles_version`).

RolePatch.description:
Request body for updating a role. Every field is optional; omitted fields are left
unchanged.

color.description: New role color as `#rrggbb`, stored as sent.

color_names.description: Whether the role colors the names of its members (see `Role.color_names`).

hoist.description:
Whether the role's members show in a group of their own in the member list (see
`Role.hoist`).

icon.description:
One emoji shown after the names of the role's members, stored as its fully-qualified
sequence (see `Role.icon`). `null` or a blank text removes it. Omit to keep it.

mask.description:
Bits covered by a permissions update. Defaults to 1023. Bits outside the mask are kept,
and set bits within 1023 are also added. Include delegated permissions in the mask to change them.

mentionable.description:
Whether anyone who can send may mention the role (see `RoleReq.mentionable`). Turning it
on needs the Mention everyone permission.

name.description: New role name: trimmed, not blank, at most 100 characters and profanity-filtered.

perms.description: New permission bitmask (see `RoleReq.perms`). Bits no role can hold are dropped.

RoleReq.description: Request body for creating a role.

color.description: Role color as `#rrggbb`, stored as sent.

mentionable.description:
Anyone who can send may mention the role (default `false`: only members with the Mention
everyone permission can). Turning it on needs the Mention everyone permission.

name.description:
Role name: trimmed, not blank, at most 100 characters and profanity-filtered. Names do
not have to be unique.

perms.description:
Permission bitmask for members with the role: 1 Manage channels, 2 Manage messages (delete
messages of others and close their polls), 4 Kick, 8 Delete server, 16 Manage admins, 32
Mention everyone and roles, 64 View audit log, 128 Timeout members, 256 Manage webhooks, 512
Manage reports, 4096 Manage server settings, 8192 Manage invites, 16384 Manage roles, 32768
Assign roles, 65536 Reset server profiles, 536870912 Pin messages and 1073741824 Bypass slow
mode,
and the bits everyone can hold (see `PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}/everyone`). Other bits
are dropped. Roles only add permissions to members who are not admins. Admins use their
own admin permissions and get only the bits everyone can hold from their roles.

RoomMetadata.description: Authorized channel identity available before opening its content.

sensitive.description: The configured channel carries a shared sensitive-content label.

RotateReq.description: What "Rotate data keys" takes: the purposes (every one when left out) and the confirmation.

purposes.description: `content`, `media`, `secrets`, `search` or `bus`; every purpose when left out.

reauth.description: How the caller confirms it is them.

Rotation.description: The rotation that runs, as kept in `settings`.

at.description: Where that step goes on: the last row it finished.

ended.description: Whether it stopped with records left, to be run again from the admin page or the CLI.

left.description: Records this pass could not seal again for now; with any, the old keys stay.

lost.description: Records under the old keys that do not open with them: they stay unreadable.

moved.description: Records this pass sealed again, or found changed meanwhile: another pass follows.

purposes.description: The purposes whose keys it replaces.

step.description: The index of the step it is at, of every step of those purposes.

RotationView.description: A rotation as the admin page shows it.

done.description: The steps this pass finished, of `steps`.

ended.description: Whether it stopped with records left.

left.description: Records this pass could not seal again for now.

purposes.description: The purposes whose keys it replaces.

waiting.description: The pass ended and the last one waits until every process can have dropped the old keys.

counts.description:
Ballots for each option still in the race (each ballot counts for its highest-ranked
option still in the race), in option order.

eliminated.description: The option eliminated after this round; `null` in the last round.

exhausted.description: Ballots that rank no option still in the race.

ends_at.description: Unix seconds; the announcement shows until just before.

ScheduleReq.description: A message to schedule. Give exactly one of `channel_id`, `dm_id` and `thread_root_id`.

at.description: When to send it (unix seconds): at least 60 seconds and at most 365 days from now.

channel_id.description: A channel to send it in.

content.description:
Its text, at most `limits.message_chars` characters: not blank, unless it carries a file
or a poll.

dm_id.description: A DM conversation to send it in.

media_alt.description: With `media_id`: a description of the image, as `SendReq.media_alt`.

media_id.description:
A file of yours from `POST /api/v1/media` to send with it, as `SendReq.media_id`. It is
kept until the message is sent, and its time before it expires starts then.

media_spoiler.description: With `media_id`: send it behind a spoiler.

mention_reply.description: With `reply_to`: ping the quoted message's author. Defaults to `true`.

oneOf.description: A poll to post, as `SendReq.poll`; `content` is ignored then. Not with `media_id`.

reply_to.description: A message of the same place to reply to, as `SendReq.reply_to`.

thread_root_id.description: The root message of a thread to reply in.

ScheduledMedia.description: The uploaded file of a scheduled message.

spoiler.description: Whether it is sent behind a spoiler.

ScheduledMessage.description: A message this site sends for you later.

at.description: When it is sent (unix seconds), as you picked it.

channel_id.description: The channel; for a thread reply in a channel, the root's channel. `null` in a DM.

created_at.description: When it was scheduled.

dm_id.description: The DM conversation; for a thread reply in a DM, the root's. `null` in a channel.

error.description: Why it failed, or `Waiting for slow mode` while slow mode holds it.

oneOf.description: The uploaded file it carries.

mention_reply.description: With `reply_to`: whether the reply pings the quoted message's author.

next_at.description:
When the server looks at it next (unix seconds): `at`, or later while slow mode holds it
or after a server failure.

oneOf.description: Names of its place you can open now; `null` when you can't open it, and in events.
Its poll, as it was given.

scope.description: Where it goes: `c<channel_id>`, `t<root_id>` for a thread reply or `d<dm_id>`.

thread_root_id.description: For a thread reply, the thread's root message.

ScheduledPage.description: A page of your scheduled messages, soonest first.
