failed.description: How many failed or are paused, with `scope` only there.

next.description: `after` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

waiting.description: How many wait to be sent (also the ones being sent), with `scope` only there.

ScheduledPatch.description: Changes to a scheduled message. Fields left out stay.

at.description: A new time (unix seconds), as for scheduling. A failed or paused message waits again.

content.description: New text: not blank, at most `limits.message_chars` characters.

remove_reply.description: `true` makes it a plain message instead of a reply.

resume.description:
`true` makes a paused message wait for its time again; one whose time passed is sent
right away. Other messages stay as they are.

ScheduledPlace.description: Names of the place of a scheduled message that you can open now.

channel_name.description: The channel's name (for a thread, its root's channel); `null` for a DM.

oneOf.description: The other person of a DM; `null` in a server.

server.description: Lowercase name of the server; `null` for a DM.

server_name.description: The server's name as shown; `null` for a DM.

ScheduledStatus.description:
Where a scheduled message is: `waiting` for its time (also while slow mode holds it, with
`error` saying so), `sending` right now, `failed` with `error` saying why, or `paused`: held
back since the account's sessions were ended, until its owner resumes it.

SealJob.description: A job over the stored messages of one place.

created_at.description: Unix seconds.

done.description: The message id it has finished up to.

from.description:
The message id before the first one of the place it covers, while it runs (0 once it
ended): how far it got is `(done - from) / (upto - from)`.

state.description: Whether it runs, ended, or stopped on an error.

upto.description: The newest message id when the job started: it covers messages up to it.

on.description: Whether new messages are stored encrypted.

SealView.description: Whether a server or DM stores new messages encrypted.

forced.description: The site requires it, so the switch can't be turned off.

on.description:
New messages are stored encrypted, by the place's own switch or because the site
requires it.

own.description: The place's own switch, whatever the site requires.

server_forced.description:
The site requires it of this server in particular; false for a DM. With
`encryption_required` of the settings, a client keeps `on` and `forced` current when only
the site-wide requirement changes.

SealedPlaces.description: How many places store new messages encrypted.

SearchResult.description: One search hit with where it was posted.

channel_name.description: Name of the channel the message is in.

message.description:
The matching message, with its link previews. It can be a thread reply (then
`thread_root_id` is set).

server.description: Lowercase name of the server the message is in.

SeatAudio.description: What a user in a voice room says about their own mic and sound.

Secret.description: A password: exactly one of `password` or `words`.

password.description: A text password (a new one must not be empty). Omit when using `words`.

words.description:
7 words, case-insensitive and in order. For a new password they must come from
`GET /api/v1/auth/words/{username}`. Omit when using `password`.

SecretReset.description: A secret reset; `url` is required when the reset makes you the owner.

SecretsReset.description: The relay or P2P secrets a start made again because the stored ones could not be opened.

pings_until.description: Highest friend ping id the client showed; all unseen ones when missing.

SendReq.description:
A new message. It needs non-blank `content` or an attachment; `media_id` and `p2p` are
mutually exclusive.

content.description:
Message text, at most `limits.message_chars` characters (Unicode code points; by default
4000, `MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS`). May be empty or blank when
an attachment is given. Up to 3 `http(s)` links in it (invite links excluded) get link
previews after the message is posted.

forward_of.description:
Optional id of a message to forward here. The server makes the new message as a copy: its
text, its server-hosted attachment (unless removed, expired, uploads are off, or 50
messages already carry that file; P2P attachments are not forwarded) and its link
previews. `forward` names the original author and time. `content`, the attachment fields
and `reply_to` are then ignored. It must be a `user` message you can read. All else, also unknown ids, gives the same
`400 Cannot forward that message`. Forwards never ping anyone.

media_alt.description:
Optional description of the attached image for people who can't see it: at most 1000
characters (code points) after cleanup (trimmed, control characters other than newlines
dropped, runs of 3 or more newlines cut to 2), checked by the profanity filter in server
channels. Blank is none. Needs `media_id` or `p2p` (`400 Image description needs an
attachment`).

media_id.description:
Optional id of a file from `POST /api/v1/media` to attach. The caller must be its uploader
and it must not already be attached to another message. Omit for no server-hosted file.

media_spoiler.description: Optional; blur the attachment behind a spoiler. Defaults to `false`.

mention_reply.description:
With `reply_to`: ping the quoted message's author (a `reply` ping, if they can see the
message and are not you). Defaults to `true`; ignored without `reply_to`.

oneOf.description:
Optional peer-to-peer attachment hosted by the sender's client instead of the server.
Omit for no P2P file.

Optional poll: the message becomes a `poll` message whose text is the question
(`content` is ignored). It cannot have an attachment. Ignored with `forward_of`.

reply_to.description:
Optional id of a message to reply to inline (quoted above the new message). It must be a
`user` message you can read in the same place: the same channel outside threads, the
same thread (or its root) for thread replies, or the same DM. Anything else, including
ids that do not exist, gives the same `400 Cannot reply to that message`.

show_source.description:
With `forward_of`: whether the copy names where the original is. `true` names its server,
and its channel when everyone in that server may see the channel; `false` names nothing
(people who can read the original still find it with
`GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/location`). Omit for the default: the channel inside its own
server, another server only when anyone may read it. A direct message is always named as
one. Ignored without `forward_of`.

Separator.description:
A decorative separator in a channel list: a line with an optional label between channels.
It is not a channel: it has no messages, voice or permissions of its own.

after.description:
How many channels of its list are above it, counting the channels the caller can see.
Separators with the same `after` keep the order they have in their list.

category_id.description: Id of the category it is listed in; `null` lists it among the channels without one.

id.description: Separator id, unique across the instance.

label.description: Text on the line, exactly as written: at most 100 characters, empty for a bare line.

SeparatorPatch.description:
Request body for changing a separator. Fields left out stay as they are. Its place changes
with `PUT /api/v1/servers/{name}/layout`.

label.description: New text on the line, as for creating one; empty for a bare line.

oneOf.description: New style.

SeparatorPlace.description: Where a separator goes in a new layout.

after.description:
How many channels of that list go above it. Separators with the same value keep the
order they are sent in.

category_id.description: Category to list it in; `null` lists it among the channels without one.

SeparatorStyle.description: How a separator line is drawn.

ServerAvailable.description: Whether a server name is free to create.

available.description: `true` when no server (public or password-protected) uses this name.

allOf.description: The banned user (their fields appear at the top level).

banned_at.description: When the ban was created, Unix seconds.

expires_at.description: When the ban ends, Unix seconds; `null` for a ban without an end.

reason.description: The reason given with the ban.

ServerBan.description: A user banned from a server.

ServerCreation.description:
Who may create servers with `POST /api/v1/servers`: `everyone`, `nobody`, or `some` (the
accounts and role holders the instance lists). `can_create_servers` in `GET /api/v1/me`
says what it means for the caller.

ServerDetail.description: A server with its channels and roles.

banner_color.description:
Background of the server-name header above the channel list as `#rrggbb`; `null`
uses the theme color.

categories.description:
Channel categories, ordered by `position`. Categories without a channel the caller can
see are left out, unless the caller manages channels.

channels.description:
Channels the caller can see, in list order (see `category_id` and `position`). Channels
where the caller lacks View channels are left out.

creator.description:
Username of the creator; `null` for the built-in `rchat` server, for a server a site
admin made for someone, and once the creator's account is deleted.

description.description:
What the server is about (see `ServerSummaryLite`). Set with
`PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`.

display_name.description: The name in its original casing.

everyone_perms.description:
The permission bits every member holds (the bits of
`PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}/everyone`). Roles add to them.

guest_chat.description: Server opt-in for guest text messages.

guest_voice.description:
"Guests can use voice": `false` keeps people without an account out of the server's
voice channels. New servers start with guest voice off. Set with
`PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`.

has_password.description: Whether joining (or viewing as a non-member) needs the server password.

hide_members.description:
Whether the server keeps its member list to its moderators (see `ServerSummaryLite`).
Set with `PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`.

icon_kind.description: How its icon is drawn (see `ServerSummaryLite`). Set with `PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`.

layout_version.description:
Version of the channel layout, for `PUT /api/v1/servers/{name}/layout` (see
`ChannelLayout.version`).

listed.description:
Whether server search lists it (see `ServerSummaryLite`). Set with
`PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`.

members_visible.description:
"Members can be seen by people outside this server" (see `ServerSummaryLite`). Set with
`PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`.

my_perms.description:
The permission bits the caller holds in the server: the bits of `Role.perms` and of
`everyone_perms`. 0 for someone who is not a member.

oneOf.description:
The caller's profile in this server; absent for non-members and while the
`server_profiles` switch is off.

name.description: Lowercase server name, the server's unique key used in URLs.

name_color.description: Color of the server name in that header as `#rrggbb`; `null` uses the theme color.

online_count.description: Number of members of this server who are online right now (anywhere on the site).

profiles_mode.description:
What members may set in their server profile: `all`, `no_names` or `off`. Set with
`PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`.

public_read.description:
"Anyone can read this server": `true` lets people who aren't members read it by its
name, `false` never does, `null` follows the instance (readable while the server has no
password and `server_joining` is `everyone`). Nobody reads it while the instance's
`public_reading` is off. Set with `PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`.

read_only.description:
Ids of listed text channels where the caller, a member, can read but not send messages
or add reactions (their own reactions can still be removed). Empty for non-members, who
cannot send anywhere.

role_limits.description: Roles the caller can't change even though the permission rules on `perms` allow it.

roles.description: Every role of the server, the highest in the role order first.

roles_order_confirmed.description:
Whether the role order decides who may moderate whom: you can kick, ban, time out or
change the roles of a member only when you rank above them, and manage a role only when
it ranks below your highest role. While `false`, moderating a member instead needs their
server permissions to be a strict subset of yours, and editing or deleting a role also
needs its permissions within yours and every other holder to be someone you could
moderate. Anyone with Manage roles turns it on with
`POST /api/v1/servers/{name}/roles/order/confirm`.

roles_version.description:
Version of the role order, for `PUT /api/v1/servers/{name}/roles/order` and
`POST /api/v1/servers/{name}/roles/order/confirm`.

seal.description: Whether new messages are stored encrypted (see `ServerSummaryLite`). Set with

separators.description:
Decorative separators of the channel list, in list order (see `Separator.after`).
Separators of categories left out are left out too.

upload_expiry.description: How long files uploaded here stay (`PUT /api/v1/servers/{name}/upload_expiry`).

upload_ttl.description:
Seconds a new file stays after upload, after the instance cap; `null` when files are kept
until removed. While `limits.upload_kept_limited` of `GET /api/v1/instance` is true, a
longer time only holds for a file that fits the kept space; else the file stays for
`limits.media_retention_secs`.

ServerEntry.description: A server to add an account to, with the roles it gets there.

roles.description: Ids of roles of that server.

ServerJoining.description:
How people get into servers by themselves: `everyone` may join any server they can open,
`invites` needs a server password or a ticket (a server without a password can't be joined
or opened by its name alone), `nobody` turns joining off (only members open servers).
Members stay in their servers either way.

ServerMatch.description: A server returned by server search.

banner_color.description: The color its icon is drawn on, as `#rrggbb`; `null` uses the theme color.

display_name.description: Server name in its original case.

has_password.description: `true` when joining the server needs a password.

icon_image.description: The id of its uploaded picture (see `ServerSummaryLite`); `null` without one.

name.description: Lowercase server name, used in URLs.

ServerOptions.description:
How a new server starts. Every field is optional; without them anyone joins the server by
its name, or with its password when `password` is set.

oneOf.description:
The channels it starts with: `text` (a text channel `general`, the default) or
`text_voice` (also a voice channel `Voice`).

How people join: `name` (anyone who knows the name), `invite` (only with an invite link
or a password the managers make), `password` (the name and `password`) or `closed`
(nobody new). Default: `password` when `password` is set, otherwise `name`. An `invite`
or `closed` server gets a random key of 10 characters for its URLs, and its name is only
a label that other servers may share. `name` is refused while the instance's
`server_joining` is `invites`.

listed.description:
Whether server search lists the server for people who aren't members while they can
read it by its name. Default `true`; `true` only for `name` and `password` servers.

notices.description: Join and leave notices in its first channel. Default `true`.

standing_link.description:
For `join: invite`: give it an invite link now, which any member may share (default
`true`); `false` leaves it to links its managers make later. Only for invite servers.

oneOf.description:
How long uploaded files stay, as in `PUT /api/v1/servers/{name}/upload_expiry`. Default:
the instance's time.

ServerPassword.description: An extra server password. Its hash and the password itself are never returned.

created_at.description: When it was created, Unix seconds.

created_by.description:
Username of the admin who created it; `null` when that account is gone or the
creator is not someone the server's members can see.

expires_at.description: When it stops working, Unix seconds; `null` for no expiry.

kind.description:
What it is: a typed or generated `password`, an invite `link`, or the server's `standing`
invite link.

label.description: Label set by the admin who created it; `null` when it has none.

max_uses.description: How many joins and guest grants it allows; `null` for unlimited.

uses.description: How many joins and guest grants used it.

ServerPasswords.description: The access settings of a server.

closed.description:
Whether the server is closed: protected, without a permanent password and without a
live extra password, so nobody new can join.

passwords.description:
Extra passwords, live ones first, then the most recent others, newest first within
each group; at most 100. Dead passwords are purged 30 days after they stopped working.

permanent.description: Whether the server has a permanent password.

protected.description: Whether joining needs a password. `false` for a public server.

ServerPatch.description:
Request body for updating a server. Every field is optional; omitted fields are left
unchanged.

banner_color.description:
Background color of the channel sidebar header as `#rrggbb` (stored lowercase). `null`
resets it to the theme color; omit to leave it unchanged.

description.description:
What the server is about, shown on invite cards and in server search: plain text, at
most 300 characters (code points) after cleanup (trimmed, control characters other than
newlines dropped, runs of 3 or more newlines cut to 2). Checked by the profanity filter
(`server_names` target). Empty or `null` clears it. Omit to keep it.

guest_chat_opt_in.description: Allow guests to send text when the site permits it.

guest_voice.description: Accepts false to disable guest voice. Enabling it requires guest_voice_opt_in.

guest_voice_opt_in.description: Allow guests to talk in voice channels when the site permits it.

hide_members.description:
"Allow members to view the member list" off (`true`): only members with Manage server,
Manage roles or Kick and ban, and instance staff, get the member list, presence and
mention suggestions; `false` (the default) leaves it to View members. Omit to leave it
unchanged.

oneOf.description:
How the server's icon is drawn: `letter` or `identicon` (see `ServerSummaryLite`). Omit
to keep it.

How people join: `name`, `invite`, `password` or `closed` (see `POST /api/v1/servers`).
Use it instead of `protected`. `password` needs `password`, unless the server has a
permanent password already. `invite` and `closed` remove the permanent password, and
`closed` revokes every extra password. A server that turns to `name` or `password`
takes its lowercase name as its key, which must be free. `name` is refused while the
instance's `server_joining` is `invites`. Not allowed on the rchat server. Omit to
leave it unchanged.

keep_guests.description:
When `password` is present, existing guest grants are revoked unless this is `true` and
`members` is `keep`. Defaults to `false`.

listed.description:
Whether server search lists the server for people who aren't members (see
`POST /api/v1/servers`). `true` only for `name` and `password` servers. Omit to leave it
unchanged.

members.description:
What to do with the other members when `password` is present: `keep` (default) or
`remove`. Ignored when `password` is omitted.

members_visible.description:
"Members can be seen by people outside this server": `false` shows the member list,
members' profiles and their membership only to other members (and the member list to
instance staff), and finds members by name through the server only for other members
(a member whose own choice is `everyone` still shows their profile and is found by
name, but not as a member), and leaves the server's `join` and `leave` messages out of
what people outside it read; `true` (the default) also for people who open the server
without being a member. Omit to leave it unchanged.

name.description:
New server name, with the same rules as when creating a server (trimmed, 1-100
characters, not `.` or `..`, profanity-filtered, not taken). Changes the lowercase `name`
used in URLs as well as the `display_name`. On the built-in rchat server only the
`display_name` changes: its key and URLs stay `rchat`.

name_color.description:
Color of the server name in the channel sidebar header as `#rrggbb` (stored lowercase).
`null` resets it to the theme color; omit to leave it unchanged.

password.description:
New permanent join password. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; a blank value removes
the permanent password, which makes the server public unless `protected` is `true`. Omit
to leave the password as it is. Not allowed on the rchat server.

oneOf.description:
What members may set in their server profile: `all` (the default), `no_names` or `off`.
Stored profiles are kept and not shown while a mode leaves them out. Omit to leave it
unchanged.

protected.description:
`false` makes the server public: the permanent password is removed and every extra
password is revoked. `true` makes it password protected; without a permanent password
and without live extra passwords it is closed (nobody new can join). Omit to keep the
current state. Not allowed on the rchat server.

public_read.description:
"Anyone can read this server": `true` lets people who aren't members read the server by
its name without joining (guests too, while guest access is on), `false` never does,
`null` follows the instance again (readable while the server has no password and
`server_joining` is `everyone`). It lets nobody join or post; readers may use its voice
channels. Omit to leave it unchanged. `true` is refused while the instance's
`public_reading` is off.

seal.description:
Whether new messages, edits and polls of the server are stored encrypted with a key this
site keeps. Messages stored before stay as they were, and turning it off decrypts
nothing. This is not end-to-end encryption. A change posts a `storage` system message.
Omit to leave it unchanged.

ServerProfile.description: The caller's profile in one server.

banner_color.description: The stored `#rrggbb` banner color; `null` uses the account's.

bio.description: The stored description; `null` uses the account's.

effective.description: How the caller shows in this server under its `mode`.

effective_banner.description: The banner color shown in this server; `null` is the default derived from the avatar.

effective_bio.description: The description shown in this server.

locked_until.description:
Until when (unix seconds) the profile can't be edited: 9223372036854775807 for a lock
that stays until a moderator lifts it; `null` when it can be edited.

mode.description: What the server lets members set.

ServerProfilePatch.description:
Changes to the caller's profile in a server. Omitted fields stay as they are; `null` goes back
to the account's value.

avatar_color.description:
`#rrggbb` color, read only together with `avatar_kind`: required for `color`, the
optional background for `identicon`.

oneOf.description: Avatar style in this server; `null` uses the whole account avatar.

banner_color.description: `#rrggbb` banner color in this server; `null` uses the account's.

bio.description:
Description shown in this server: at most 190 characters, checked by the profanity filter
(`bios` target). Empty or `null` uses the account's.

name.description:
The name shown in this server, under the rules of the account's display name. A name
equal to the account's display name is stored as `null`.

ServerResult.description: What became of one server of the request.

error.description: Why the account was not added.

server.description: The server as the request named it.

ServerSummary.description: A server the signed-in user is a member of.

banner_color.description:
Background of the server-name header above the channel list as `#rrggbb`; `null`
uses the theme color.

creator.description:
Username of the creator; `null` for the built-in `rchat` server, for a server a site
admin made for someone, and once the creator's account is deleted.

display_name.description: The name in its original casing.

icon_kind.description: How the server's icon is drawn (see `ServerSummaryLite`).

is_admin.description: Whether the signed-in user is an admin of this server.

name.description: Lowercase server name, the server's unique key used in URLs.

name_color.description: Color of the server name in that header as `#rrggbb`; `null` uses the theme color.

profiles_mode.description: What members may set in their server profile: `all`, `no_names` or `off`.

timed_out_remaining.description:
Seconds left of that timeout when the response was made (count down from this, so a
device clock that is off does not matter).

timed_out_until.description: When your timeout in this server ends (unix seconds), while you are timed out.

ServerSummaryLite.description: Public facts about a server, without membership details.

banner_color.description:
Background of the server-name header above the channel list as `#rrggbb`; `null`
uses the theme color.

creator.description:
Username of the creator; `null` for the built-in `rchat` server, for a server a site
admin made for someone, and once the creator's account is deleted.

description.description: What the server is about: plain text, at most 300 characters; `null` without one.

display_name.description: The name in its original casing.

guest_chat.description: Server opt-in for guest text messages.

guest_voice.description:
"Guests can use voice": `false` keeps people without an account out of the server's
voice channels. Accounts are not affected.

has_password.description: Whether joining (or viewing as a non-member) needs the server password.

hide_members.description:
"Allow members to view the member list" off: only members with Manage server, Manage
roles or Kick and ban (and instance staff) see who is in the server, their presence and
mention suggestions. While `false`, View members (34359738368) decides, per channel.

icon_kind.description:
How its icon is drawn: `letter` (the first letter of its name, the default) or
`identicon` (a pattern made from its key), on its `banner_color` when it has one.

join_mode.description:
How people join: `name` (anyone who knows its name), `invite` (with an invite link, or
a password the managers made), `password` (its name and its password) or `closed`
(nobody new). `has_password` is `true` for every mode but `name`.

listed.description:
Whether server search lists it for people who aren't members, while anyone can read it
by its name. Only servers people join by name (`name` and `password`) are ever listed.

members_visible.description:
"Members can be seen by people outside this server": `true` (the default) lets people
who can open the server without being a member see its member list and its members'
profiles and find them by name through it; `false` shows them only to members (and the
member list to instance staff), and people outside the server get none of its `join`
and `leave` messages. A member whose own choice is `everyone` still shows their profile
and is found by name, but not as a member of this server.

name.description: Lowercase server name, the server's unique key used in URLs.

name_color.description: Color of the server name in that header as `#rrggbb`; `null` uses the theme color.

profiles_mode.description: What members may set in their server profile: `all`, `no_names` or `off`.

public_read.description:
"Anyone can read this server": `true` lets people who aren't members read it by its
name, `false` never does, `null` follows the instance (readable while the server has no
password and `server_joining` is `everyone`). Nobody reads it while the instance's
`public_reading` is off.

seal.description:
Whether new messages of the server are stored encrypted with a key this site keeps
(this is not end-to-end encryption), and whether the site requires it. Set with
`PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}`. Older servers send nothing, which reads as off.

allOf.description: The server as it is after the update (its fields appear at the top level).

kept.description: Number of members other than the caller who are still in the server.

removed.description: Number of members removed because `members` was `remove`; 0 otherwise.

ServerUpdated.description: The server after an update, plus how many members a password change removed.

Session.description: An origin-bound session for this widget.

mode.description: Access mode used to offer the appropriate sign-in or password form.

ticket.description: Short-lived credential scoped to this widget configuration and parent origin.

Settings.description:
Instance-wide feature switches. Changes reach clients through the `settings_changed`
WebSocket event. A switched-off feature's endpoints answer 404, except that uploads, P2P
attachments, outgoing webhooks and new scheduled messages answer 403, guests get 401 while
guest access is off, and `client_other_instances` gates no endpoint. What `server_creation`, `server_joining` (under
`nobody`), `server_search`, `dm_creation` and `friend_requests` refuse carries `reason` with
kind `off_site` and the setting's key as `control`; an account that `server_creation: some`
leaves out gets `off_account`.

animated_profile_pictures.description:
Whether an animated upload keeps its animation (under `profile_pictures`). Off: an
upload keeps only its first frame, `GET /api/v1/avatars/{id}/{size}/animated` answers
404, and clients draw the stills.

asset_previews.description: Link previews: the server fetches page metadata for links in messages.

builtin_server.description:
Whether the instance still has its built-in server `rchat`: `kept`, or `removed` once
the instance deleted it. While it is kept, its key and URL stay `rchat`, it takes no
password, and only its display name changes on a rename.

calls.description:
Voice channels and DM calls that run through the instance. Off: joining a voice channel
and starting or accepting a call are refused with a WebSocket `error` frame whose
`reason` is `off_site` with control `calls`, and running calls end. Voice channels stay.
P2P calls follow `p2p` instead.

client_other_instances.description:
Adding other instances in the web app this instance serves. Only that app reads it:
the desktop and mobile apps and other web apps ignore it, and it gates no endpoint.

docs.description:
The documentation site at `/docs`. While off, every `/docs` page answers 404 with a
page that says so.

e2ee_compliance.description: The compliance archive in new encrypted spaces. Off by default.

friend_requests.description:
New friend requests. Off: `POST /api/v1/friends/requests` answers 404, except that it
still accepts a request the other user sent. Pending requests can be accepted or
denied, and friends stay.

guest_chat_enabled.description: Site permission for servers to opt in to guest chat.

guest_voice_enabled.description: Site permission for servers to opt in to guest voice.

guests_enabled.description: Guest access: reading servers without an account.

incoming_webhooks.description:
Incoming webhooks. Off: creating one, resetting its token and every request to a
webhook URL (`/api/v1/webhooks/{id}/{token}`) answer 404 `Not found` with reason
`off_site` and control `incoming_webhooks`. Existing webhooks stay, are still listed,
and work again when it is back on.

interactive_docs.description:
Whether the docs this instance serves, and the docs the apps carry, may run requests as
the accounts the app holds on this instance. Only the docs read it; it gates no endpoint.

member_lists.description:
Member lists: who is in a server, their presence and mention suggestions. While off,
nobody but instance staff gets a server's member list; existing servers and members stay.

outgoing_webhooks.description:
Outgoing webhooks: servers may have the instance POST signed event payloads to URLs
their managers choose. Off by default (`OUTGOING_WEBHOOKS`); while off, nothing
is queued or sent and outgoing webhooks cannot be created.

p2p.description:
Peer-to-peer servers and conversations in the app this instance serves. Off: the app
hides them, and `POST /api/v1/identity/p2p_binding` and P2P backup uploads answer 404.
Data on devices and stored backups are kept.

p2p_attachments.description:
Peer-to-peer attachments: files hosted by the sender's browser, without a size limit.
With this and `asset_uploads` off the instance is text only: messages carrying any
attachment are rejected and existing ones are no longer offered.

p2p_backup.description:
Uploads of P2P backups (`PUT /api/v1/me/p2p_backup/{ik}`). Off: uploads answer 404; stored
backups can still be read and deleted.

password_change.description:
What an account that signed in with a temporary password must do: `required` (its
sessions can only change the password, read the account and sign out; everything else
answers 403 `Change your password first`) or `encouraged` (it works as usual until the
temporary password expires, then as under `required`). `required` by default
(`TEMP_PASSWORD_CHANGE`).

password_login.description:
Password sign-in. Off: no new passwords (see `registration`); existing passwords still
sign in.

profanity_filter.description:
Master switch of the profanity filter. Off by default (`PROFANITY_FILTER`).
When on, content matching a target in `profanity_targets` is rejected with 400
`Content blocked by profanity filter`.

profanity_strict_file_names.description:
While the filter checks `file_names`: file names, and file names in the paths of links in
any checked text, are also read whole, like message text. Off by default
(`PROFANITY_STRICT_FILE_NAMES`): a known extension is read apart from the name before it.

profanity_targets.description: Which texts the filter checks while `profanity_filter` is on.

profile_choices.description:
What an account's own `profile` choice does: `any` (it applies, wider or narrower than
`profile_visibility`), `narrower` (only a narrower one applies; a wider one acts as no
choice) or `site` (every account follows `profile_visibility`; choices are kept). `any` by
default (`PROFILE_CHOICES`).

profile_pictures.description:
Whether accounts may upload a profile picture (`PUT /api/v1/me/avatar`) and pictures
are served. Off: uploads answer 403 with reason `off_site`, `GET /api/v1/avatars/...`
answers 404, and clients draw the built-in avatars. A picture can still be removed.

profile_visibility.description:
Who may see an account's profile (its description, banner color and creation time):
`everyone`, `public_servers` (everyone, for an account in a server anyone can read;
others as `shared`) or `shared` (people who share a server, a direct conversation the
account wrote in or a friendship with it). `shared` by default (`PROFILE_VISIBILITY`).
Never `friends`, which only an account chooses for itself (`profile` in
`GET /api/v1/me/privacy`).

public_reading.description:
Whether servers can be read by people who aren't members: a server is readable by its
name when its own `public_read` is `true`, or `null` while the server has no password
and `server_joining` is `everyone`. Off: no server is, whatever its option says, and
`PATCH /api/v1/servers/{name}` refuses `public_read: true` with reason `off_site`.

registration.description:
Who may create an account with a password: `open`, `sso` (only through single
sign-on) or `closed`. `POST /api/v1/auth/register` answers 404 unless it is `open` and
`password_login` is on.

scheduled_messages.description:
Scheduled messages: people may have this site send a message for them at a time they
pick (`POST /api/v1/me/scheduled`). Off: no new ones (403 with reason `off_site`); those
already scheduled still send, and can be edited, sent now or deleted.

server_creation.description:
Who may create servers: `everyone`, `nobody` or `some` (listed accounts and role
holders; the list is not public). `POST /api/v1/servers` answers 404 to everyone else.
Existing servers are not affected.

server_joining.description:
How people get into servers by themselves: `everyone`, `invites` (only with a server
password or a ticket: without one, every name gets the answers of a password-protected
server) or `nobody` (joining and guest access requests answer 404). Members stay.
Reading follows it: under `invites` and `nobody` a server without a password is closed
to everyone who is not a member, like a password-protected one, and server search
leaves it out. Under `nobody` a request without a password is not asked for one: it
gets the 404 of a wrong password.

server_profiles.description:
Server profiles: a name, avatar, banner color and description a member sets for one
server. While off, the `/api/v1/servers/{name}/profile` endpoints answer 404 and no
response carries a server profile; stored profiles are kept.

sfu.description:
Calls through the instance's media server when it runs (`sfu` in `GET /api/v1/instance`).
Off by default.

temp_password_hours.description:
How many hours a new temporary password signs in for: 1 to 720, or 0 for no expiry. 72
by default (`TEMP_PASSWORD_HOURS`). A temporary password keeps the expiry it was issued
with.

upload_expiry_max_days.description:
Longest upload expiry a server may choose, in days: 1 to 365, or 0 for no cap (servers
may then also keep files until they are removed). Longer choices are shortened to it.
0 by default (`UPLOAD_EXPIRY_MAX_DAYS`).

widget_bridge.description: Widgets for P2P servers through the instance's bridge. Off by default.

widget_chat.description: Sending from widgets, and Quick join.

SettingsPatch.description:
Request body of `PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings`: the settings to change. A field left out stays
as it is.

app_name.description: The name the app shows for itself.

app_short_name.description: The short name of the app, for home screens.

asset_previews.description: Link previews: the server fetches page metadata for links in messages.

brand_about.description: The text of the About section.

brand_links.description: The links of the About section.

calls.description:
Voice channels and DM calls that run through the instance. Off: joining a voice channel and
starting or accepting a call are refused with a WebSocket `error` frame whose `reason` is
`off_site` with control `calls`, and running calls end. Voice channels stay. P2P calls
follow `p2p` instead.

client_other_instances.description:
Adding other instances in the web app this instance serves. Only that app reads it: the
desktop and mobile apps and other web apps ignore it, and it gates no endpoint.

default_servers.description: Keys of the servers new accounts join, in order.

oneOf.description:
Who may start a direct conversation: `everyone`, `friends` (only with a friend) or `nobody`.
`POST /api/v1/dms` answers 404 for a conversation it would have to create; conversations
that exist, and the self DM, keep working.

e2ee_compliance.description: The compliance archive in new encrypted spaces. Off by default.

friend_requests.description:
New friend requests. Off: `POST /api/v1/friends/requests` answers 404, except that it still
accepts a request the other user sent. Pending requests can be accepted or denied, and
friends stay.

guest_chat_enabled.description: Site permission for servers to opt in to guest chat.

guest_voice_enabled.description: Site permission for servers to opt in to guest voice.

guests_enabled.description: Guest access: reading servers without an account.

incoming_webhooks.description:
Incoming webhooks. Off: creating one, resetting its token and every request to a webhook URL

`incoming_webhooks`. Existing webhooks stay, are still listed, and work again when it is
back on.

oneOf.description: The instances the app suggests when adding one.

interactive_docs.description: Running requests from the docs as the app's accounts.

login_note.description: A note shown on the sign-in page.

member_lists.description: Member lists: who is in a server, their presence and mention suggestions.

outgoing_webhooks.description:
Outgoing webhooks: servers may have the instance POST signed event payloads to URLs their
managers choose. Off by default (`OUTGOING_WEBHOOKS`); while off, nothing is queued or sent
and outgoing webhooks cannot be created.

scheduled_messages.description: Scheduled messages this site sends for people later.

server_creators.description: Usernames that may create servers while `server_creation` is `listed`.

server_profiles.description: Server profiles: a name, avatar, banner and description per server.

sfu.description:

widget_bridge.description: Widgets for P2P servers through the instance's bridge. Off by default.

widget_chat.description: Sending from widgets, and Quick join.

SharedConfig.description: The config string behind a share link.

blob.description: The encoded config string, as uploaded.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working, Unix seconds.

ShownSource.description: What a forward that shows where it is from may name.

channel.description:
Name of the channel, without `#`, when everyone in the server may see it; absent
otherwise.

SnapFile.description: The file a reported message carried: its name, type and size, never its content.

SnapMessage.description: A message as it was when the report was sent. Later edits and deletes don't change it.

oneOf.description: Who wrote it; `null` for a webhook's post.

created_at.description: When it was sent, unix seconds.

edited_at.description: When it was last edited before the report, unix seconds.

oneOf.description: The file it carried.

thread_root_id.description: The thread it is a reply in.

webhook.description: The name a webhook posted it under.

SnapServer.description: A reported server as it was when the report was sent.

description.description: Its description, when it had one.

display_name.description: The name in its original casing.

has_password.description: Whether joining it needed a password.

name.description: The server's name, its key.

public_read.description: Its "Anyone can read this server" option: `null` followed the instance.

SnapUser.description:
A person as a report keeps them: the names they had when the report was sent. Once the
account is deleted only `deleted` is left.

deleted.description: The account was deleted after the report.

display_name.description: The display name at the time.

Snapshot.description: What a report keeps of its target, taken when it was sent.

channel.description: The name of the channel the message was in.

context.description:
Up to 10 messages before it from the same channel, thread or direct conversation,
oldest first, when the reporter chose to include them.

oneOf.description: The reported message.
The reported server.
The reported account.

remaining.description: Seconds from now until it closes, for a client whose clock differs from the server's.

until.description: Unix seconds until which the channel stays open to the admin.

reauth.description:
How the admin confirms: the account password or words, a `phrase` proof (purpose
`staff_view`, context the channel id as decimal text) or a fresh provider sign-in.

StartChannels.description:
The channels a new server starts with: `text` (a text channel `general`) or `text_voice`
(also a voice channel `Voice`).

StoredAnswer.description:
An answer as a report keeps it, with the field's label and the labels of the chosen options
at report time, so later changes of the form never change what an old report says.

label.description: The field's label when the report was sent.

shown.description: For choices: the labels of the chosen options when the report was sent.

value.description:
The answer: a string for text fields and a single choice, a list of option ids for a
multiple choice, `true` for a checkbox, and for a reference the names it had:
`{"username", "display_name"}`, `{"server", "display_name"}` or
`{"message_id", "author"}`. `{"deleted": true}` stands for an account deleted since.

Suggestion.description: An instance the app suggests when someone adds one.

label.description: Up to 32 characters; may be empty.

url.description: The instance's address: an `http` or `https` origin.

SuggestionMode.description: Whether the instance's suggestions come after the app's own list or replace it.

mode.description: `add` (after the list the app was built with) or `replace` (instead of it).

SystemMessages.description: Join and leave message settings of a server.

channel_id.description:
Text channel that gets join and leave messages; `null` for the default channel (the
server's first text channel). A deleted channel falls back to the default.

join_messages.description: Whether a message is posted when someone joins (not for guests).

leave_messages.description: Whether a message is posted when a member leaves, is kicked or is banned.

SystemMessagesPatch.description: Changes to the join and leave message settings. Omitted fields stay unchanged.

channel_id.description: A text channel of the server you can see, or `null` for the default channel.

join_messages.description: Turns join messages on or off.

leave_messages.description: Turns leave messages on or off.

Target.description: What a report is about: `kind`, and the values that kind takes.

kind.description: What kind of thing it is.

TargetKind.description: What kind of thing a report is about.

TempChange.description:
What an account that signed in with a temporary password must do: `required` (its sessions
can only change the password, read the account and sign out) or `encouraged` (it works as
usual until the temporary password expires, then as under `required`).

TempView.description: The temporary password an account signed in with, in `GET /api/v1/me`.

change.description:
What applies to this session right now: `required` (it can only change the password,
read the account and sign out; also once the temporary password has expired) or
`encouraged`.

expires_at.description: When the temporary password stops signing in (unix seconds); null for never.

TemporaryPassword.description: The temporary password of an account in the account view.

expires_at.description: When it stops signing in (unix seconds); null for never.

ThreadItem.description: A thread: its root message and its newest reply.

last_reply_at.description: When the newest reply was sent, Unix seconds.

root.description: The root message as message lists show it; `reply_count` counts its replies.

ThreadPings.description: Unseen pings of one thread in a scope.

pings_until.description: Highest unseen ping id among them.

TicketReq.description: Request a one-time ticket for a provider flow.

oneOf.description: Confirmation for linking a new identity.

TicketResp.description: Single-use ticket to pass to the start endpoint.

ticket.description: Opaque ticket valid for five minutes.

TimeoutReq.description: Request body for timing out a member.

reason.description: Why, shown to moderators and in the audit log; at most 300 characters.

seconds.description: How long the timeout lasts from now, 1 second to 28 days (2419200).

Unread.description: Read position of one channel or DM.

group_pings.description:
Unread messages in this channel that ping the caller through `@everyone`, `@here` or a
role they hold, newest first (not included in `pings`; at most 1000 over all scopes).
They stop counting once the read position reaches them. Empty for DMs.

last_read.description: Last message id the caller marked read with `POST /api/v1/read`; 0 if never.

latest.description: Id of the newest top-level message from someone else (thread replies are not counted).

pings.description:
Unseen pings (mentions, replies and reactions for the caller) in this scope, including
its thread replies. A scope with pings is listed even when it is read.

pings_until.description:
Highest unseen ping id outside threads (0: none). Send it as `pings_until` to
`POST /api/v1/read` for this scope.

scope.description: `c<channel id>` for a text channel or `d<dm id>` for a DM.

server.description: Lowercase server name for a channel scope; `null` for a DM.

thread_pings.description:
Unseen pings on thread replies in this channel or DM, per thread (included in `pings`).
Read with scope `t<root id>`.

UnreadCount.description: The messages from others after a position in a channel or DM.

latest.description: Id of the newest one counted; `null` when there are none.

since.description: Unix seconds of the first one; `null` when there are none.

Unreads.description: The caller's unread channels and DMs.

items.description:
Unread scopes, newest `latest` first and at most 500. With `all=true`: every scope with
messages from others, read or not, in no particular order and without a cap.

more.description:
`true` when more than 500 scopes were unread and the list was cut; always `false` with
`all=true`.

Updated.description:
What a `message_updated` carries: the whole message (DMs, call logs), or for an edit in a
server channel only which message changed, so viewers without read history of it learn
nothing; clients holding it re-read it through the gated REST list.

UploadExpiry.description: A server's choice for how long uploaded files stay.

seconds.description:
Seconds after upload for `custom`, 3600 (1 hour) to 31536000 (365 days); `null`
otherwise.

UploadExpiryState.description: A server's upload expiry and what it means for new files now.

oneOf.description: After a change: what it did to the files already posted. Left out when reading.

The kept space of the account charged for this server's longer choice, across all
servers it is charged for, which a file must fit too. `null` when nobody is charged: the
server keeps nothing longer, or the account that set its choice is gone and nobody has
set it since. Such a server has only its own kept space.

upload_ttl.description:
Seconds new files stay after upload, after the instance cap; `null` when they are kept
until removed. A file that does not fit the kept space stays for the instance default.

UserCard.description: An account's card: its name, and the parts the caller may see.

oneOf.description:
Membership in the server given by `server`; null when `server` was omitted, the caller
may not view it, or the user is not a member.
The profile; null when the account does not show it to the caller.

user.description: The user's public identity and avatar.

UserRef.description:
A user as shown next to messages and in lists. A deleted account still appears, as its
username on a grey color avatar.

avatar_color.description:
Avatar color as lowercase `#rrggbb` when `avatar_kind` is `color`. For identicons it is
the chosen background color, or `null` for the default background.

avatar_image.description:
The id of the user's uploaded profile picture, served at
`GET /api/v1/avatars/{id}/{size}`; `null` without one. The avatar of `avatar_kind` is
what shows until the picture has loaded, and when it is not shown.

display_name.description: The name shown for the user: the username as registered until they change it.

username.description: Lowercase username, the user's unique key.

messages.description: Readable top-level chat history, oldest first.

name.description: Channel name.

participate.description: Whether the viewer may send text or join voice here.

users.description: Voice participants visible to this viewer.

View.description: The single channel and controls available to this viewer.

VoteReq.description:
A vote. Send `options` for `single`, `multiple`, `ranked` and `yes_no`, `value` for
`rating`.

options.description:
Option ids: exactly one for `single` and `yes_no`, `min_choices` to `max_choices`
different ones for `multiple`, and for `ranked` one or more different ones, best first
(options left out are unranked).

Webhook.description: An incoming webhook as its managers see it. The token is never included.

avatar_kind.description: How its default avatar is drawn.

created_at.description: When it was created, Unix seconds.

oneOf.description: Who created it; `null` once that account is gone.

id.description: Webhook id, the first part of its URL.

mentions.description:
Whether it may use `@everyone`, `@here` and role mentions (`allowed_mentions` still has
to ask): its creator could when they created it. Checked again on every message.

name.description: Default name of its messages.

New text, at most `limits.message_chars` characters (by default 4000,
`MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS`).

embeds.description: New embeds (replacing the old ones), at most 10; `[]` removes them.

WebhookInfo.description: What an incoming webhook may say through its token.

avatar_kind.description: How its default avatar is drawn.

name.description: Default name of its messages.

WebhookPatch.description: Changes to an incoming webhook; omitted fields stay.

avatar_color.description: `#rrggbb`, required for `color` unless it already has one.

oneOf.description: How its default avatar is drawn.

channel_id.description:
Move it to this text channel (at most 15 webhooks per channel by default,
`CHANNEL_WEBHOOKS_MAX`).

name.description: 1 to 80 characters, checked like a new name.

token.description: The secret part of its URL. Shown only now; only a keyed hash is stored.

WebhookSecret.description: A webhook with its token, returned once when it is created or its token is reset.

read_key.description: A read link's revocable key, visible only to managers.

Widget.description: A managed widget and its current configuration.

composer.description: Allow text entry when the viewer may post.

origins.description: Allowed HTTP or HTTPS parent origins. An empty list permits public framing.

WidgetPost.description: Result of sending text from the widget.

session.description: Server-scoped guest credential for later sends, absent for accounts.

WordsResp.description: The candidate words of a word-password account.

words.description: 20 distinct lowercase words, derived deterministically from the lowercase username.

oneOf.description:
Messages of one channel, thread (`thread_root_id`) or DM deleted together by a bulk
delete; ids only. A viewer without read history of some of them gets only the ids it
could read (`created` is routing only).

A role's name, color, icon, mention setting or how it shows changed; its permissions did
not.

The rank order or the display order of a server's roles changed. `order` lists every
role, the highest first, and `display` the display position of each in the same order.
A member was given or lost a role: `role_ids` are the roles they hold now.
The server's upload expiry changed; clients load the server again.

The permission rules of several channels changed at once (a category's rules reached the
channels that copy them).

Who is in a voice channel now. In the snapshot a connection gets when it opens or
subscribes, `audio` also lists what each of them not at the default says about their own
mic and sound; changes after that come as `voice_audio`.

A user in a voice channel is muted there (a timeout, or no Speak permission in the
channel), or no longer is; or, with `staff`, staff muted a guest for everyone in the
server's voice, or ended that. Apps stop sending and playing a muted user's audio.

What a user in a voice channel says about their own mic (`muted`) and sound (`deafened`)
changed.

A timeout of `username` in `server` started or changed (`until`, `remaining` seconds and
the reason) or ended (`until` null). Only to that user and to members with the Timeout
members permission; the user's own copy has no reason unless they hold it too.

The name or avatar `username` shows in `server` changed: `profile` is the look now, null
when they use the account's. `bio` says their description or banner color there changed:
ask for the card again. To the server and to that user.

The reports of `server` changed, or without one the reports to the instance: ask for the
open count again. Only to the members of the server who hold Manage reports, or to
whoever handles the instance's reports. It never says what changed, and it never goes
to someone who can't see the report that changed: the account it is about (`about`),
or a moderator who can't view the channel of its message (`channel`: its id and
whether it was private).

answered_at.description: Active calls only: when the call was answered, in unix seconds.

call_id.description: Active P2P calls only: the call's id, which the caller puts in the PeerJS metadata.

peers.description: Active P2P calls only: the peer id of the caller's tab and of the tab that accepted.

relays.description:
P2P calls only: relay hosts a side declared (the caller's while ringing, both once
active), so the other side can ask before it connects through them.

video.description: The caller started with video on.

oneOf.description: The name a guest connection has in voice rooms, sent to it first.
Whether the DM stores new messages encrypted changed; to its participants only.
`username` closed the DM; to that user's connections only.
The DM is back in `username`'s list; to that user's connections only.

`username` marked these group-mentioned messages of channel `scope` seen in the inbox
(at most 1000 ids); to that user's connections only.
`username` blocked a user; to that user's connections only.
`username` unblocked `blocked`; to that user's connections only.

`username` voted in or took back their vote in poll `message_id`; to their own
connections only, so their other tabs load the poll again.
Progress of `username`'s bulk delete job; to their own connections only.

`username`'s scheduled message was scheduled, edited, held by slow mode or failed; to
their own connections only. Its `place` is always null.

`username`'s scheduled message `id` is gone: deleted, or sent as `sent_message_id`; to
their own connections only.

The site admin `username` confirmed opening channel `channel_id` as staff; to their own
connections only, so they deliver its events until it closes.

Progress of a job over stored messages `username` started; to their own connections
only.

A friend request between `username` and `request.user` was sent or arrived; to
`username`'s connections only.

The friend request between `username` and `other` is gone (accepted, denied or
cancelled); to `username`'s connections only.
`friend.user` is now a friend of `username`; to `username`'s connections only.
`friend` is no longer a friend of `username`; to `username`'s connections only.

`friend` (a friend of `username`) came online or went offline; to `username`'s
connections only.
`username` changed their privacy settings; to that user's connections only.

Internal, never delivered: `username` became visible on the site (`online`), or stopped
being visible (after the offline grace, or at once when they appear offline). The hub's
replica emits it on every instance (`Hub::take_shown`), and each instance tells the
friends connected to it (`friend_presence`).
The instance's brand changed: its names, texts, links, suggested instances or images.

Answer to `p2p_hosting`, to that connection only: which of the `checked` ids are still
live P2P attachments of the sender, so its app stops serving removed ones.

key.description: Hex key the hoster checks download tokens with, valid for `peer_id`.

now.description: Server time in unix seconds, so the hoster can check token expiry on a skewed clock.

oneOf.description:
Answer to `p2p_peer`, to that connection only: where to fetch the attachment of
`message_id` and the token for it, or `error`.

relays.description: Relay hosts the hoster declared for this file.

oneOf.description:
Someone is typing in `scope` (`c{channel}`, `t{root}` or `d{dm}`) until `until` (unix
seconds), or stopped when `until` is 0. Never sent to the typer's own connections.

bearer.description: A session token from `POST /api/v1/auth/register`, `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, `POST /api/v1/auth/recovery` or `POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/exchange`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens do not expire; `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` revokes one, a password change revokes all others, and a recovery revokes every earlier one. An unknown token on an endpoint that also allows guests is treated as no token.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Incoming webhooks post into one text channel through a secret URL (no account, no bot user), with a WEBHOOK badge. Outgoing webhooks POST signed JSON events of a server to a URL, only when the instance allows them. Outgoing payloads look like `{id, webhook_id, type, server, created_at, data}`; verify `X-Webhook-Signature` (`sha256=` plus the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `<X-Webhook-Timestamp>.<raw body>` under the secret) and reject the request when `|now - X-Webhook-Timestamp|` is over 300 seconds. `X-Webhook-Delivery` stays the same across retries: use it as the idempotency key. Each try is built from current data as the webhook's owner may see it then: an edited message is sent with its current content, a message deleted before its delivery went out arrives as `message.deleted`, and nothing is sent once the owner lost access. The owner is whoever created the webhook or last changed what it receives (URL, events, turning it on, a new secret; for incoming webhooks a new URL or another channel). Events: `message.created` and `message.updated` (`data.message`), `message.deleted` (`data.channel_id`, `thread_root_id`, `ids`), `member.joined` (`data.user`), `member.left` (`data.username`, `kicked`, `banned`), `reaction.added` and `reaction.removed` (`data.message_id`, `channel_id`, `emoji`, `user`, `count`), `poll.ended` (`data.message`), and `ping` from the test button.
